There is no shortage of options.
"We have a very good understanding of the needs of our football team," Newsome said. "What we try to do is to match that with the players."
Some things to know about the Ravens' draft:
TIGHT END NEEDED
The leading receiver on the team last season was tight end Benjamin Watson, who joined the Saints as a free agent.
A replacement is sorely needed, and after failing to secure one through free agency, the Ravens will look to snag one in the draft.
"There are some pretty good ones out there. And they're of the athletic variety, pass-catching tight ends that certainly could help impact our offence," said Joe Horitz, director of college scouting.
One of Newsome's best picks was tight end Todd Heap, selected in the first round in 2001 even though the Ravens already had future Hall of Fame star Shannon Sharpe.
TRADE OR NOT?
Newsome cryptically mentioned the possibility of trading the No. 16 pick, but DeCosta likes the idea of drafting in the middle of the round.
"We're in a good spot for a lot of different reasons," DeCosta said. "I think 16 is a good spot to be in this draft. It plays well to our needs and different strategies."
VOLCANO BREWING
Coach John Harbaugh has been in the Ravens draft room since 2008, and when it comes time for Baltimore to make a pick, he just gets out of the way.
"I'll tell you, it's like a volcano, kind of. It's festering, like, 'Is this thing going to blow?' It never quite blows, but there's so much tension," Harbaugh said.
In the end, though, it's Newsome's call.
"Ozzie pulls the trigger and makes a decision," Harbaugh said, "and we all feel good about it."
HITS, MISSES AND BARGAINS
Perriman missed the entire 2015 season with a knee injury, caught 33 passes in 2016 and last season had a mere 10 catches for the league's 29th-ranked passing attack.
Newsome also struck out with safety Matt Elam at No. 32 overall in 2013. But he recently found two fourth-round gems: Defensive end Brent Urban in 2014 and offensive lineman Alex Lewis in 2016.
___
For more NFL coverage: http://www.pro32.ap.org and http://www.twitter.com/AP_NFL
By David Ginsburg, The Associated Press
rewrite:
The Ravens enter the draft with a clear plan and no shortage of options. "We have a very good understanding of our team's needs," said General Manager Ozzie Newsome. "Our job is to match those needs with the right players."

Here are some key points to understand about Baltimore's approach:

**A Pressing Need at Tight End**
The departure of last season's leading receiver, tight end Benjamin Watson, to free agency has created a significant void. Having not addressed the position in free agency, the Ravens are expected to target a tight end in the draft. "There are some pretty good ones available," said Joe Hortiz, the director of college scouting. "They're the athletic, pass-catching type who could really impact our offense." Newsome has a history of success at this position, famously selecting Todd Heap in the first round in 2001 despite already having future Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe on the roster.

**To Trade or Not to Trade?**
Newsome has hinted at the possibility of trading the 16th overall pick, but Assistant General Manager Eric DeCosta sees value in staying put. "We're in a good spot for a lot of reasons," DeCosta noted. "I think 16 is a good position to be in this year. It aligns well with our needs and allows for various strategies."

**A Draft Room 'Volcano'**
Head Coach John Harbaugh, a fixture in the draft room since 2008, described the tense atmosphere when Baltimore is on the clock. "It's like a volcano brewing," Harbaugh said. "There's this festering tension, like, 'Is this thing going to blow?' It never quite does, but the pressure is palpable." Ultimately, however, the final decision rests with Newsome. "Ozzie pulls the trigger and makes the call," Harbaugh added, "and we all feel good about it."

**A Mixed Record of Hits and Misses**
The draft is an inexact science, as the Ravens' recent history shows. Wide receiver Breshad Perriman, a first-round pick in 2015, missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury and has struggled to produce consistently since. Newsome also missed on safety Matt Elam, a first-round selection in 2013. However, he has also uncovered late-round bargains, such as defensive end Brent Urban (2014) and offensive lineman Alex Lewis (2016), both found in the fourth round.

Over time, however, Edmonton’s location — and, in particular, the lack of direct flights from New York — came to feel like a plus, rather than a minus.
Advertisement Continue reading the main story
“There was something attractive about doing it in a place where there wouldn’t be a whole set of eyes seeing the work and judging it before it’s fully baked,” Ms. Chavkin, who had never been to Edmonton and had never heard of Citadel, said.
Then there was the money.
The American dollar stretches further in Canada. And Citadel was not asking for much — the theater agreed to spend what it usually spends to stage a musical (about $600,000 Canadian) and also agreed not to seek a royalty from future productions (nonprofits that help develop commercial shows often get a percentage of Broadway profits).
The commercial producers would pay the rest of the costs, and bring their own sound and lighting equipment, a revolving stage, and significant set elements to upgrade what they would find at Citadel.
Photo
“There was no question it was financially in our interest to go to Canada,” said Ms. Isaacs, who is producing the show along with Mr. Kirdahy, Dale Franzen, and Hunter Arnold.
During just three weeks of rehearsal and four previews, Ms. Chavkin restaged the show several times over, with new cast members, including Reeve Carney (“Spider-Man: Turn Off the Dark”), in three of the five main roles. At first, a rail line bisected the stage; the creative team scrapped that design after a single performance. There were several experiments with how best to deploy characters added for the Edmonton production in an effort to bring to life, as it were, those toiling away in hell.
“We’re trying to walk this line between maintaining the metaphorical and poetic world, and also trying to deliver a satisfying story,” Ms. Mitchell said. “The only way we know where it comfortably wants to sit is by going too far in one direction or another.”
The Citadel says that if it worked on a Broadway-aimed show again, it would dedicate a staffer to managing relations with the commercial producers, because immigration and budget issues proved more time-consuming than anticipated.

Over time, Edmonton’s remote location—especially the absence of direct flights from New York—began to seem like an advantage rather than a drawback. “There was something appealing about developing the work in a place where it wouldn’t be scrutinized by a whole crowd of eyes, judged before it was fully realized,” explained Ms. Chavkin, who had never visited Edmonton nor heard of the Citadel Theatre before. Another compelling factor was financial. The American dollar goes further in Canada, and the Citadel’s ask was modest: the theater agreed to cover its typical musical production budget (around $600,000 Canadian) and forgo any royalty from future stagings—unlike many nonprofits that help develop commercial shows and often receive a share of Broadway profits. The commercial producers would cover the remaining costs, bringing in their own sound and lighting equipment, a revolving stage, and major set pieces to enhance what was available at the Citadel.

“Financially, going to Canada was unquestionably in our interest,” said Ms. Isaacs, who is producing the show alongside Mr. Kirdahy, Dale Franzen, and Hunter Arnold. During a compact period of just three weeks of rehearsals and four preview performances, Ms. Chavkin repeatedly reworked the staging, integrating new cast members—including Reeve Carney (“Spider-Man: Turn Off the Dark”) in three of the five principal roles. An initial design that split the stage with a rail line was abandoned after only one performance. The creative team also experimented with how to best use additional characters introduced for the Edmonton production, aiming to vividly portray those laboring in hell. “We’re trying to walk this line between preserving the metaphorical, poetic world and delivering a satisfying narrative,” Ms. Mitchell noted. “The only way to find where the story comfortably wants to sit is by pushing too far in one direction or another.”

Reflecting on the experience, the Citadel noted that if it undertakes another Broadway-bound production, it would assign a dedicated staff member to manage relations with commercial producers. Immigration logistics and budget matters turned out to be more time-consuming than expected, highlighting the need for focused coordination.

An employee stands outside a Lowe's home improvement chain in Austin, Texas, U.S., February 27, 2017. REUTERS/Mohammad Khursheed
NEW YORK Shares of home improvement retailer Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW.N) could rise by 20 percent or more, helped by better projected earnings growth this year and greater room for margin improvement, Barron's said on Sunday.
Companies such as Lowe's and Home Depot Inc (HD.N) are uniquely positioned due to their strong outlook, as a healthy economy and improving real estate markets in most of the United States encourages homeowners to undertake renovation, Barron's said.
These companies are also "Amazon proof", the report said, noting that home improvement was low on the list of categories the retailer is expected to penetrate.
U.S. retail heavyweights including Target Corp (TGT.N), Wal-Mart Stores Inc (WMT.N) and Kroger Co (KR.N) have been locked in a fierce battle against Amazon Inc (AMZN.O).
While both Home Depot and Lowe's are poised for growth, Lowe's could be more attractive now, due in part to its lower price-to-earnings ratio, the report said.
Lowe's shares trade at $82, or about 18 times projected earnings of $4.63 per share for year ending January 2018, while Home Depot trades at $147, or 20.4 times estimated earnings of $7.19 per share in its current year, Barron's said.
Lowe's same-store sales performance has lagged Home Depot's the past several quarters, mainly due to its focus on do-it-yourself customers who spend less on big-ticket items than professionals.
However, the retailer is taking steps to boost per-store revenue, which would help narrow the valuation gap, Barron's said.
Lowe's offers investors exposure to one of retail's strongest sectors, the potential for 15 percent annual earnings growth and a "shareholder friendly" management, according to the report.
(Reporting by Devika Krishna Kumar in New York; Editing by Meredith Mazzilli)

Shares of home improvement retailer Lowe’s Companies Inc could see gains of 20 percent or more, according to a Sunday report from Barron’s. The projection is based on stronger expected earnings growth this year and significant room for margin improvement. The report noted that companies like Lowe’s and Home Depot Inc are well positioned due to a favorable economic environment. A healthy U.S. economy and improving real estate markets in most regions are encouraging homeowners to invest in renovations.

Barron’s also described these home improvement retailers as “Amazon proof,” observing that this category is relatively insulated from Amazon’s expansion. While other major U.S. retailers such as Target, Walmart, and Kroger are engaged in intense competition with Amazon, home improvement remains lower on the list of sectors the online giant is expected to penetrate deeply.

Although both Home Depot and Lowe’s are poised for growth, Lowe’s may currently offer a more attractive opportunity, partly due to its lower price-to-earnings ratio. Lowe’s shares trade around $82, or about 18 times projected earnings of $4.63 per share for the year ending January 2018. In comparison, Home Depot trades near $147, or 20.4 times estimated earnings of $7.19 per share for its current fiscal year.

Lowe’s same-store sales have trailed Home Depot’s in recent quarters, largely because Lowe’s has focused more on do-it-yourself customers, who typically spend less on big-ticket items than professional contractors. However, Barron’s highlighted that Lowe’s is implementing measures to increase revenue per store, which could help close the valuation gap with its rival. The report added that Lowe’s gives investors exposure to one of retail’s strongest segments, the potential for 15 percent annual earnings growth, and a management team committed to shareholder returns.

A proposed Snowboard and Freeski Big Air World Cup competition due to take place in Düsseldorf next season has been postponed for a year due to a scheduling conflict.
The event had been scheduled to be held on a temporary ramp in the Espirit Arena in January, the same venue which hosted the World Table Tennis Championships last year.
Organisers have determined, however, that there will be "insufficient time to realise the construction of the competition ramp" in the 54,000 capacity venue due to other events also taking place there.
"Because of this, the decision was made to postpone the event from the 2018/19 season until the 2019/20 World Cup season, where the safety of the athletes can remain paramount and the true vision for the competition can be fully realised," said the International Ski Federation (FIS).
"At this time the proposed schedule for the Düsseldorf Snowboard and Freeski big air World Cup will see the competition held from January 2 to 4, 2020."
The Big Air event in Düsseldorf had been due to take place in the Espirit Arena ©SOP Architekten
The Big Air World Cup season is due to begin in Cardrona in New Zealand in September and continue with events in Milan, Beijing, Canyons in United States, Quebec and Oslo.
"While the cancellation of this season’s Dusseldorf event is disappointing for all parties involved, excitement for the 2020 event is high as the FIS snowboard and freeski tours look forward to bringing World Cup big air action to one of the great cities of Europe," FIS added.
"With Düsseldorf 54,000 seat Espirit Arena - home to the Fortuna [football team who recently earned promotion to the Bundesliga for the 2018/19 season] - lined up to host the competition, the Düsseldorf snowboard and freeski big air competitions are set to be season highlights in January 2020."
rewrite:

The competition was originally set for next season on a temporary ramp inside the Espirit Arena in January—the same venue that hosted the World Table Tennis Championships last year. Organizers concluded there would be "insufficient time to realise the construction of the competition ramp" within the 54,000-seat arena because of other events booked at the location.

The International Ski Federation (FIS) explained the decision: "Because of this, the event has been postponed from the 2018/19 season to the 2019/20 World Cup season. This will ensure the safety of the athletes remains paramount and allow the full vision for the competition to be realised." According to the updated plan, the Düsseldorf Big Air World Cup is now scheduled to run from January 2 to 4, 2020.

While acknowledging the disappointment caused by rescheduling this season’s Düsseldorf event, FIS expressed strong anticipation for the 2020 edition: "Excitement for the 2020 event is high as the FIS snowboard and freeski tours look forward to bringing World Cup big air action to one of the great cities of Europe."

The Espirit Arena—home to Fortuna Düsseldorf, the football team recently promoted to the Bundesliga for the 2018/19 season—will provide a major stage for the event. With its 54,000-seat capacity, the venue is expected to help make the Düsseldorf snowboard and freeski big air competitions standout highlights of the January 2020 calendar.

MIAMI (WFLA) – CarePlus Health Plans is notifying customers after a privacy breach that occurred on Jan. 17.
The breach occurred due to a series of programming and printing errors, resulting in Explanation of Benefits letters being mailed to the incorrect CarePlus member.
The EOBs impacted with the errors were mailed out on Jan. 9 and Jan. 16. Roughly 11,200 members’ information as sent to another member.
Personal financial information and Social Security numbers were not contained in the letters.
The information disclosed included:
Member name
CarePlus identification number and plan name
Date(s) of service(s)
Provider of service
Services provided
CarePlus has no information that any data has been inappropriately used.
Anyone who notices any changes in their EOB statement, SmartSummary or medical records that are unfamiliar to them, or customers who have any questions, should contact CarePlus at 1-800-794-5907, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
WHAT OTHERS ARE CLICKING ON RIGHT NOW:
rewrite:

The affected EOBs were sent on January 9 and 16, involving approximately 11,200 members whose information was mistakenly directed to another individual.

The letters did not contain sensitive personal financial details or Social Security numbers. Recently it was reported that the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Scuba Club lost their official University recognition. A "risk assessment" deemed the clubs too risky. What a shame! The Caving Club has sponsored regular trips for 70 years; the Outing Club is nearly 100 years old.
What has changed over the past 100 years that would cause Penn State University to take such a drastic step? Lawsuits, lawyers, and a whole lot of money.
According to student leaders of these organizations, losing campus recognition means a club will no longer be covered under the university's $1 million liability insurance policy. I will put it more bluntly: It is too risky for Penn State to continue insuring these clubs because of the constant threat of lawsuits. That pot of a million bucks is just too attractive to plaintiffs' attorneys. The propensity to sue in our overly litigious society puts Penn State and any large organization with deep pockets right in the cross hairs of lawyers.
While some might blame Penn State for being too cautious, the university is not really to blame here. It must make these decisions mindful that attorneys are always looking for the chance to strike. And it's not just "dear old State." Thanks to abusive lawsuits, entire industries have disappeared in Pennsylvania and the cost of goods and services continue to rise as the explosive costs of litigation are factored in. Penn State and its students are just the most recent victims.
It begs the question: Where will the plaintiffs' attorneys strike next? Perhaps the table tennis club?
Curt Schroder
Executive director, Pennsylvania Coalition for Civil Justice Reform
Hatrisburg
rewrite:
Recent reports confirm that the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club, and Scuba Club have lost their official university recognition, deemed too hazardous following a risk assessment. This is a genuine loss: the Caving Club has organized regular excursions for seven decades, and the Outing Club is nearly a century old. What has shifted over the past hundred years to prompt such a drastic move? In a word: litigation. Lawsuits, lawyers, and considerable financial exposure have driven this decision.

According to student leaders, losing recognition strips these clubs of coverage under the university’s $1 million liability insurance policy. To put it bluntly, Penn State now views insuring these groups as too risky due to the persistent threat of lawsuits. That million-dollar pool is simply too tempting for plaintiffs’ attorneys. In our overly litigious society, the tendency to sue places Penn State—and any large institution with deep pockets—directly in the crosshairs of legal action.

While some may criticize the university for excessive caution, Penn State isn’t the true culprit here. It must make these decisions knowing that attorneys are constantly seeking opportunities to strike. And this isn’t just about “dear old State.” Abusive lawsuits have wiped out entire industries in Pennsylvania, while the soaring costs of litigation drive up prices for goods and services. Penn State and its students are merely the latest casualties.

This raises a pressing question: where will plaintiffs’ lawyers target next? Perhaps the table tennis club?

Curt Schroder  
Executive Director, Pennsylvania Coalition for Civil Justice Reform  
Harrisburg

After shocking the football community in 2017 and nearly defeating the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship, it appears the bookies over in Vegas are still somewhat skeptical about the Jacksonville Jaguars. In the latest early odds by Las Vegas Super Book, that was exactly the case as they gave the Jags 20-to-1 odds with six other teams.
Odds to win next year's Super Bowl, via @LVSuperBook: Patriots (4-1)
Steelers (8-1)
Eagles (10-1)
Vikings (12-1)
Packers (12-1)
Saints (16-1)
Falcons (18-1)
Cowboys/Rams/Seahawks/49ers/Jaguars/Texans (20-1) — Will Brinson (@WillBrinson) January 29, 2018
What’s interesting about Super Book’s odds is that the Pittsburgh Steelers, who the Jags beat twice at Heinz Field, are ranked way ahead of the Jaguars with 8-to-1 odds. Something else that will grab the attention of Jags fans is that the Seahawks, who missed the playoffs and were defeated by the Jags, also have 20-to-1 odds.
One reason for the Jags’ questionable odds could be due to the strength of schedule in 2018, which will be much more difficult than 2017’s. Also, it appears Vegas is skeptical on the Jags’ play at quarterback despite Blake Bortles improving this season. That said, it appears the odds above favor teams with elite quarterback play.
Needless to say, these odds could drastically change with the free agency and the draft coming up in March and April. We’ll be sure to check the odds all throughout the offseason to mark the Jags’ progress in the eyes of Vegas.
rewrite:
Despite their stunning run in 2017, which included nearly toppling the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship, the Jacksonville Jaguars still aren't getting full respect from Las Vegas bookmakers. The latest early odds from the Las Vegas Super Book place the Jaguars at 20-to-1 to win Super Bowl LIII, a tier they share with six other teams.

The posted odds list the Patriots as 4-1 favorites, followed by the Steelers at 8-1. What stands out is that Pittsburgh, a team the Jaguars convincingly beat twice last season—including at Heinz Field—is ranked far ahead of them. Also notable is that the Seattle Seahawks, who missed the playoffs and lost to Jacksonville, share the same 20-to-1 line.

Several factors likely contribute to this skepticism. The Jaguars face a significantly tougher strength of schedule in 2018 compared to their breakout year. Furthermore, Vegas seems doubtful about the team's quarterback situation; despite clear improvement from Blake Bortles this past season, the odds notably favor franchises with established elite passers.

Of course, these early numbers are far from final. The upcoming free agency period and the NFL draft in March and April will dramatically reshape rosters and, consequently, the betting lines. We'll be tracking the odds throughout the offseason to gauge how the Jaguars' perceived prospects evolve in the eyes of the oddsmakers.

MELBOURNE Australia pace spearhead Mitchell Starc and batsman Chris Lynn have been named as part of a formidable squad for next month's Champions Trophy in England and Wales despite nursing injuries.
Starc was forced to pull out midway through the India tour last month with a fractured foot while Lynn has been sidelined with a shoulder injury during the Indian Premier League.
Both are expected to be fit for Australia's opener on June 2 against New Zealand.
"Our medical staff will continue to monitor Mitchell and Chris’s recovery from their respective injuries but we are hopeful they will be fit in time for the team’s departure on May 18,” selector Trevor Hohns said in a media release.
James Faulkner, man-of-the-match in the 2015 World Cup final against New Zealand, has been omitted from the 15-man squad named on Thursday, with selectors opting for all-rounders Moises Henriques, Glenn Maxwell and Marcus Stoinis.
Young fast bowler Pat Cummins and James Pattinson, on the comeback trail after suffering stress fractures in his back, were included in an imposing pace battery along with Josh Hazlewood and John Hastings.
"Both James and John have made very good returns from injury and are bowling well for their respective teams in the English county competition as well as both contributing well with the bat," Hohns said.
"When you also add Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins to the fast bowling artillery it becomes a very exciting proposition for Australian cricket."
Legspinner Adam Zampa is the sole specialist spinner in the squad, while batsmen Usman Khawaja, George Bailey and Peter Handscomb have missed out.
World champions Australia, who lost their top ranking to South Africa earlier this year, will bid for their third win in the quadrennial one-day international tournament after back-to-back triumphs in 2006 and 2009.
Squad:
Steve Smith (captain), David Warner, Pat Cummins, Aaron Finch, John Hastings, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Moises Henriques, Chris Lynn, Glenn Maxwell, James Pattinson, Mitchell Starc, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, Adam Zampa
(Reporting by Ian Ransom; Editing by Amlan Chakraborty/Peter Rutherford)
rewrite:
Despite nursing injuries, Australian pace spearhead Mitchell Starc and explosive batsman Chris Lynn have been included in a formidable 15-man squad for next month’s Champions Trophy in England and Wales. Starc was forced to withdraw midway through last month’s tour of India with a fractured foot, while Lynn has been sidelined with a shoulder injury during the Indian Premier League. Both are expected to be fit for Australia’s tournament opener against New Zealand on June 2.

Selector Trevor Hohns, in a media release, expressed confidence in their recovery: "Our medical staff will continue to monitor Mitchell and Chris’s recovery from their respective injuries, but we are hopeful they will be fit in time for the team’s departure on May 18."

Notably omitted from the squad is James Faulkner, the man-of-the-match in the 2015 World Cup final. Selectors have instead opted for all-rounders Moises Henriques, Glenn Maxwell, and Marcus Stoinis. The pace attack looks particularly imposing, featuring Josh Hazlewood, John Hastings, and the returning Pat Cummins and James Pattinson—the latter making a comeback after stress fractures in his back.

Hohns highlighted the depth of the fast-bowling unit: "Both James [Pattinson] and John have made very good returns from injury and are bowling well for their respective teams in the English county competition, while also contributing with the bat. When you add Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, and Pat Cummins to the fast-bowling artillery, it becomes a very exciting proposition for Australian cricket."

Leg-spinner Adam Zampa is the sole specialist spinner in the squad, while batsmen Usman Khawaja, George Bailey, and Peter Handscomb have missed selection. As reigning world champions, though recently displaced from the top ODI ranking by South Africa, Australia will aim for a third Champions Trophy title, having won the tournament back-to-back in 2006 and 2009.

**Squad:** Steve Smith (captain), David Warner, Pat Cummins, Aaron Finch, John Hastings, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Moises Henriques, Chris Lynn, Glenn Maxwell, James Pattinson, Mitchell Starc, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, Adam Zampa.

MORRIS, Minn. — A 94-year-old Minnesota man whose wife died after battling cancer built a swimming pool in his backyard for children in his neighborhood.
Keith Davison’s wife of 66 years died last year, KARE 11 reports.
“You just can’t imagine what it’s like,” he said. “You cry a lot. That’s just the way it is because she’s not here.”
Davison then decided to do something different to fill his time.
In the spring, the retired judge had an in-ground pool built. In July, the pool, which is 32 feet long and 9 feet deep, opened — and kids from all over the neighborhood came to swim.
“I knew they’d come,” Davison said.
Davison, who has three adult children but no grandchildren, is usually seen sitting in a chair next to the pool, watching the kids swimming, laughing and having fun.
“I’m not sitting by myself looking at the walls,” Davison said. “What else would you think of doing where you could have a whole bunch of kids over every afternoon?”
rewrite:
In Morris, Minnesota, a 94-year-old man found a unique way to cope with the loss of his wife after her battle with cancer: he built a backyard swimming pool for the neighborhood children. Keith Davison, whose wife of 66 years passed away last year, described the profound loneliness he faced. “You just can’t imagine what it’s like,” he said. “You cry a lot. That’s just the way it is because she’s not here.”

Seeking to fill his time, the retired judge had an in-ground pool constructed this spring. By July, the 32-foot-long, 9-foot-deep pool was open, quickly drawing children from all around. “I knew they’d come,” Davison remarked.

Though he has three grown children but no grandchildren, Davison now spends his afternoons sitting beside the pool, watching the kids swim and laugh. “I’m not sitting by myself looking at the walls,” he explained. “What else would you think of doing where you could have a whole bunch of kids over every afternoon?”

Champion Austin Rogers is the second hit on a Google search for Jeopardy! right now. Why? Because he's a refreshing no-holds-barred contestant on the famously dry TV game show.
The gregarious Rogers is a New York City-based bartender with a 70's anchorman look who's made headlines of late, thanks to his wacky demeanor and subsequent success: he racked up $69,000 in a single episode, and has been the show's champion for the last eight nights with winnings totaling $306,900.

But it's his charisma—not so much his winning streak—that's enchanted viewers on the internet:

Over the course of his still-going eight-episode run, Rogers has deadpanned his way through nearly every correct answer with the finesse of a comedian.
Alex Trebek introduced the champion best: "He's got hair, he's got chutzpah, and broad-based knowledge. He's got quite the showman in him."
You can watch Rogers ham it up on 'Jeopardy!' tonight at 7pm EST.
rewrite:
If you search for Jeopardy! online right now, contestant Austin Rogers is one of the first results to appear. The reason? He’s a refreshingly bold presence on a show often known for its serious tone. Rogers, a gregarious New York City bartender with a 1970s news-anchor style, has recently captured attention with his quirky personality and impressive winning streak. He earned $69,000 in a single episode and, after eight consecutive nights as champion, has amassed total winnings of $306,900.

Yet what has truly captivated viewers online is less his streak and more his natural charisma. Throughout his ongoing eight-episode run, Rogers has delivered nearly every correct answer with the dry wit of a seasoned comedian. Host Alex Trebek summed him up perfectly: “He’s got hair, he’s got chutzpah, and broad-based knowledge. He’s quite the showman.” You can catch Austin Rogers in action on Jeopardy! tonight at 7 p.m. EST.

Salt Bae was invited to the Laureus World Sports Awards this year. The annual ceremony recognizes ” the most remarkable men and women from the world of sport along with their achievements” (if you don’t know who Salt Bae is skip to below the video and read that first).
While Salt Bae was there, he salted the food of Olympic gold medalist gymnast and Laureus World Sportswoman of the Year Simone Biles. Biles and her mom clearly loved it.
got my food salted by the one & only 😂 #Laureus17 pic.twitter.com/Wf2iIQ1Nr5 — Simone Biles (@Simone_Biles) February 14, 2017
If you’re wondering who the heck “Salt Bae” is, I’ll explain. His real name is Nusret Gokce, and he’s a Turkish chef who owns steak restaurants. He went viral because of the way he sprinkles salt in this video.
Ever since then, he has been salting food for famous people like Leonardo DiCaprio and other athletes like Rickie Fowler.
Life’s good for Salt Bae.
The 'salt bae' phenomenon has hit the sporting world. It makes sense that the man who started it all – chef Nusret Gokce – is at #Laureus17 pic.twitter.com/VA9U6SDnbX — CNN Sport (@cnnsport) February 14, 2017
It’s amazing what can happen when you go viral on the Internet!
rewrite:
This year, the Laureus World Sports Awards—an annual ceremony honoring the world’s most remarkable athletes and their achievements—featured an unexpected guest: Salt Bae. While attending the event, the internet-famous chef seasoned a meal for Olympic gold medalist and Laureus World Sportswoman of the Year Simone Biles, much to the delight of both Biles and her mother.

For those unfamiliar, Salt Bae is the online persona of Turkish chef and restaurateur Nusret Gokce. He rose to viral fame through a video showcasing his dramatic, smooth technique for sprinkling salt. Since then, he has become a pop-culture sensation, personally seasoning dishes for celebrities such as Leonardo DiCaprio and athletes like golfer Rickie Fowler.

His appearance at the awards underscores how his quirky brand of showmanship has permeated even the elite sporting world. As social media continues to propel unexpected figures into the spotlight, Salt Bae’s journey from chef to viral celebrity reminds us just how unpredictable—and entertaining—internet fame can be.

By Liana B. Baker and Olivia Oran
April 12 Morgan Stanley's chief compliance officer Billy Fenrich is leaving the firm just over a year after being named to the position.
Fenrich will be replaced by Raul Yanes, according to an internal Morgan Stanley memo reviewed by Reuters, which was confirmed by a firm spokesman.
Fenrich is joining quantitative hedge fund AQR Capital Management as its chief legal officer, according to an AQR spokeswoman.
Yanes was most recently a litigation partner at the law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell and had also served in a number of senior positions under president George W. Bush, including staff secretary and assistant to the president and senior counselor to the attorney general.
Fenrich joined Morgan Stanley's legal department in 2014 from hedge fund PointState Capital. He was named chief compliance officer in 2016, replacing longtime compliance chief Stuart Breslow. He had also worked at Davis Polk.
Compliance officers have become critical figures on Wall Street since the financial crisis, helping to ensure that bankers and traders stay out of trouble and avoid massive fines. (Reporting by Liana Baker and Olivia Oran in New York; Editing by Tom Brown)
rewrite:
Morgan Stanley’s chief compliance officer, Billy Fenrich, is departing the firm just over a year after his appointment, according to sources familiar with the matter. He will be succeeded by Raul Yanes, as stated in an internal memo reviewed by Reuters and confirmed by a company spokesperson. Fenrich is set to join quantitative hedge fund AQR Capital Management as its chief legal officer.

Yanes, who most recently served as a litigation partner at Davis Polk & Wardwell, brings extensive public service experience, having held several senior roles during the George W. Bush administration, including staff secretary and assistant to the president.

Fenrich originally joined Morgan Stanley’s legal team in 2014 from hedge fund PointState Capital. He ascended to the chief compliance officer role in 2016, taking over from longtime compliance head Stuart Breslow. Notably, Fenrich also previously worked at Davis Polk.

In the years following the financial crisis, compliance officers have grown into pivotal positions across Wall Street, tasked with guiding firms away from misconduct and shielding them from substantial regulatory penalties.

HOLLYWOOD stars including Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, and Chelsea Handler were forced to evacuate their homes as the deadly fire in California continues to burn.
President Donald Trump has declared a state of emergency and ordered federal agencies to help with rescue efforts.
White House spokeswoman Lindsay Walters said Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue briefed Trump and Vice President Mike Pence on a wildfire prevention roundtable today.
Walters said the White House “continues to closely monitor the situation” and is urging “anyone ordered to evacuate during a wildfire, do so immediately and listen to your local and state officials”.
Camera Icon Firefighters monitor a blaze beside Highway 33 near Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP Camera Icon Firefighters comb through smouldering ash in the remains of dozens of homes destroyed by the Lilac Fire in San Diego. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
She also said the White House “extends its thoughts and prayers” to everyone affected by the fires that have been tearing through Southern California.
Authorities today issued new alerts about unhealthy air from smoke and ash sent up by the growing wildfire.
Celebrities including former Glee star Lea Michele, talk show host DeGeneres, along with Hilton and Kylie Jenner were forced to flee their homes and, in Jenner’s case, her Kylie Cosmetics headquarters.
Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery restaurant in the foothill enclave of Montecito, said customers were wearing masks.
Camera Icon Flames erupt on mountainsides in the Los Padres national forest north of Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
He said smoke was so thick that visibility was down to a few metres and a layer of ash was coating the streets.
Regulators were warning resident in parts of Santa Barbara, Ventura and Los Angeles counties to stay indoors, avoid vigorous outdoor activities and not do anything to stir up ash.
Even residents of Montecito and neighbouring Carpinteria who weren’t under evacuation orders opted to leave because of the thick blanket of smoke.
rewrite:
As deadly wildfires continue to rage across California, numerous Hollywood celebrities, such as Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, and Chelsea Handler, have been compelled to evacuate their homes. In response to the crisis, President Donald Trump has declared a state of emergency, directing federal agencies to assist in rescue operations. White House spokeswoman Lindsay Walters reported that Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue briefed both President Trump and Vice President Mike Pence during a wildfire prevention roundtable. Walters emphasized that the White House is "closely monitoring the situation" and urged all residents under evacuation orders to heed local and state officials and leave immediately. She added that the administration extends its "thoughts and prayers" to everyone impacted by the blazes sweeping Southern California.

Authorities have issued new alerts regarding unhealthy air quality caused by smoke and ash from the expanding fires. Among the celebrities forced to flee were former *Glee* star Lea Michele, talk show host Ellen DeGeneres, along with Paris Hilton and Kylie Jenner—who also evacuated her Kylie Cosmetics headquarters. In the foothill community of Montecito, Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery, noted that customers were wearing masks due to the severe conditions. He described smoke so dense that visibility was reduced to just a few meters, with a layer of ash covering the streets.

Regulators have warned residents in parts of Santa Barbara, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties to remain indoors, avoid strenuous outdoor activities, and refrain from any actions that might stir up ash. Even in areas like Montecito and neighboring Carpinteria, where evacuation was not mandatory, many chose to leave because of the thick, hazardous smoke. Meanwhile, firefighters continue their arduous efforts, monitoring blazes along Highway 33 near Ojai and combing through the smoldering remains of homes destroyed by the Lilac Fire in San Diego, as flames persist in the Los Padres National Forest.

A World War One grave in France marked as that of an unknown soldier has been identified as the resting place of an army officer from Scotland.
The headstone at Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, near Reims, was dedicated only to "a major" of the Royal Engineers.
Detective work by David Tattersfield, of the Western Front Association, identified the major to be an Alexander Soutar, a minister's son.
Maj Soutar was born in Cullen and grew up in Glasgow and Thurso.
He fought at the Somme in 1916 and Passchendale in 1917, before being shot and killed by a sniper on 28 May 1918 while helping to defend the village of Hermonville, near Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, from an attack by German soldiers.
One hundred years after his death, Maj Soutar's descendants have gathered at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission Cemetery where he lies to honour him.
A new headstone with his name has been erected.
rewrite: A World War One grave in France, long marked as that of an unknown soldier, has now been identified as belonging to a Scottish army officer. The headstone at Jonchery-sur-Vesle, near Reims, was originally inscribed only to "a major" of the Royal Engineers. Through meticulous detective work by David Tattersfield of the Western Front Association, the major was identified as Alexander Soutar, the son of a minister. Born in Cullen, Maj Soutar grew up in Glasgow and Thurso. He fought at the Somme in 1916 and Passchendaele in 1917 before being shot and killed by a sniper on May 28, 1918, while helping defend the village of Hermonville from a German attack. One century after his death, his descendants gathered at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery to honor him, where a new headstone bearing his name has been erected.

ROCHESTER, Mich. — Tai Odiase had 19 points, on 8-for-8 shooting, and three blocks, Godwin Boahen hit four 3-pointers and finished with 16 points and Illinois-Chicago beat Oakland 79-73 on Friday night for its fifth win in a row.
Marcus Ottey added 15 points and Tarkus Ferguson had 13 points, nine rebounds and seven assists for UIC (13-11, 8-3 Horizon League). The Flames have eight conference wins for the first time since finishing the 2007-08 season 9-9 in Horizon League play.
Odiase had a dunk and two layups during a 6-2 spurt that made it 17-14 and UIC led the rest of the way. Ferguson converted a 3-point play to spark a 10-2 run that pushed the lead to 11 points before Boahen's 3-pointer made it 40-30 at the break. Nick Daniels hit a 3 that pulled Oakland (14-10, 6-5) within two points with two minutes to play, but Ottey made two free throws and Odiase hit a jumper to make it 76-69 and UIC made 4 of 6 free throws in the final 32 seconds to seal it.
Martez Walker had 21 points and Jalen Hayes scored 15 for Oakland. Kendrick Nunn added 20, but shot 3 of 22 from the field, including 1 of 10 from 3-point range.
rewrite:
ROCHESTER, Mich. — Illinois-Chicago extended its winning streak to five games with a 79-73 victory over Oakland on Friday night. Tai Odiase led the Flames with a perfect 8-for-8 shooting performance, scoring 19 points and adding three blocks. Godwin Boahen contributed 16 points, hitting four three-pointers. Marcus Ottey chipped in 15 points, while Tarkus Ferguson filled the stat sheet with 13 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists.

The win improves UIC to 13-11 overall and 8-3 in the Horizon League, marking the first time the Flames have reached eight conference wins since the 2007-08 season. UIC took control early after a 6-2 run, capped by Odiase, gave them a 17-14 lead they would not relinquish. A 10-2 surge, sparked by a three-point play from Ferguson, helped build an 11-point advantage, and Boahen’s three-pointer sent UIC into halftime up 40-30.

Oakland (14-10, 6-5) rallied late, with Nick Daniels hitting a three to close within two points in the final two minutes. But Ottey sank two clutch free throws and Odiase hit a key jumper to push the lead to 76-69, and UIC sealed the win by making four of six free throws in the last 32 seconds.

For Oakland, Martez Walker scored 21 points and Jalen Hayes had 15. Kendrick Nunn added 20 points but struggled from the field, shooting just 3 for 22, including 1 of 10 from beyond the arc.

The Center for Law and Social Justice at Medgar Evers College is a winner of the Brooklyn Community Foundation’s Annual Spark Prize, which recognizes exceptional nonprofits rooted in Brooklyn that advances racial and social justice. The center will receive $100,000 in general operating support from the foundation.
CLSJ is one of five organizations receiving the prestigious Spark Prize, along with the Cave Canem Foundation, Exalt Youth, GRIOT Circle and the Red Hook Initiative. The organizations, each receiving $100,000, were selected from a pool of over 130 applicants by a 30-member committee of Brooklyn leaders in business, civics and philanthropy. All will be honored February 8 at a celebration breakfast hosted by actress and comedian Ana Gasteyer that includes a tribute to Hildy J. Simmons, a philanthropic leader and longtime Brooklyn Community Foundation board member.
“We are absolutely thrilled to be selected as a winner of the Spark Prize Award,” said Esmeralda Simmons, Esq., founder and executive director of CLSJ. “It is our mission to advocate for and assist African descendant and disenfranchised communities on racial justice issues such as voter rights, educational inequity, police violence, as well as tackling issues that impact women of color, and this award will help us further that mission.”
The Brooklyn Community Foundation is dedicated to Brooklyn’s charitable community and partners with donors and community leaders to bolster nonprofits, strengthen neighborhoods and increase opportunities for youth. Simmons expressed gratitude to Foundation President and CEO Cecilia Clarke for aiding social justice initiatives in Brooklyn. She also thanked the Brooklyn community for their continued support.
Medgar Evers College’s renowned Center for Law and Social Justice provides advocacy, training and expert services in a personal manner. CLSJ conducts research and initiates advocacy projects and litigation on behalf of community organizations and groups that promote human, national and international understanding.
The Spark Prize, sponsored by TD Bank with support from National Grid, is presented by the Brooklyn Community Foundation in partnership with the Office of the Brooklyn Borough President and the Brooklyn Chamber of Commerce.

The Center for Law and Social Justice at Medgar Evers College has been named a winner of the Brooklyn Community Foundation’s annual Spark Prize, an award honoring exceptional nonprofits deeply rooted in Brooklyn that advance racial and social justice. CLSJ is one of five organizations to receive the prestigious prize this year, alongside the Cave Canem Foundation, Exalt Youth, GRIOT Circle, and the Red Hook Initiative. All five will be honored at a celebration breakfast on February 8, hosted by actress and comedian Ana Gasteyer. The event will also include a tribute to Hildy J. Simmons, a philanthropic leader and longtime Brooklyn Community Foundation board member.

“We are absolutely thrilled to be selected as a winner of the Spark Prize,” said Esmeralda Simmons, Esq., founder and executive director of CLSJ. “Our mission is to advocate for and assist African descendant and disenfranchised communities on racial justice issues—from voter rights and educational inequity to police violence—while also tackling challenges that disproportionately impact women of color. This award will help us further that vital work.”

Simmons expressed gratitude to Foundation President and CEO Cecilia Clarke for her commitment to social justice initiatives across the borough, and thanked the broader Brooklyn community for its ongoing support.

The Spark Prize is presented by the Brooklyn Community Foundation in partnership with the Office of the Brooklyn Borough President and the Brooklyn Chamber of Commerce. The award is sponsored by TD Bank with additional support from National Grid.

FORD COUNTY – One person was injured in a 3-vehicle accident just after 4p.m. on Tuesday in Ford County.
The Kansas Highway Patrol reported a 2016 Dodge Ram pickup driven by Jessee Stickell, 51, Pottsville, PA., was northbound on U.S. 56 just south of U.S. 400.
As the pickup approached the intersection at Lariat Way, a 2001 Cadillac DeVille driven by Jose G. Soto-Gonzalez, 30, Dodge City, attempted to cross U.S. 56 from Lariat Way.
The Dodge collided with the Cadillac and rolled into the northeast ditch. The Cadillac spun around and hit a USD 443 school bus driven by Wade S. Hampton, 64, Dodge City, that was stopped on Lariat Way headed west bound on U.S. 56.
Stickel was transported to Western Plains Medical Center.
Soto-Gonzalez, Hampton and 9 children on the school bus were not injured.
The drivers were properly restrained at the time of the accident, according to the KHP.
rewrite: One person was injured in a three-vehicle crash Tuesday afternoon in Ford County. The Kansas Highway Patrol reported the accident occurred shortly after 4 p.m. A 2016 Dodge Ram pickup, driven by 51-year-old Jessee Stickell of Pottsville, Pennsylvania, was traveling north on U.S. 56 just south of U.S. 400. As it approached the Lariat Way intersection, a 2001 Cadillac DeVille, driven by 30-year-old Jose G. Soto-Gonzalez of Dodge City, attempted to cross the highway from Lariat Way. The Dodge struck the Cadillac and rolled into the northeast ditch. The impact caused the Cadillac to spin and collide with a stopped USD 443 school bus, driven by 64-year-old Wade S. Hampton of Dodge City, which was on Lariat Way waiting to turn west onto U.S. 56. Stickell was taken to Western Plains Medical Center. Soto-Gonzalez, Hampton, and the nine children on the bus were unhurt. The KHP confirmed all drivers were wearing seatbelts.

We live in a society where people are quite judgmental about how a woman dresses or behaves. Sadly, in our country, a smoking and tattooed women are still considered promiscuous.
Kriti Sanon is all set to question this stigma with her role of Bitti in her upcoming film Bareilly Ki Barfi. Talking about it, the actress was quoted as saying, "Smoking is not good for health and should be avoided. I am a non-smoker, but the point we want to make is that girls who smoke, who are fond of body art or break into a jig are not characterless."
She further added, "Our society has a very small bracket for 'good girls'. That bracket needs to broaden up or change. When a guy is moophat or smokes, he is not considered characterless, but you judge girls too fast. This is seen more in smaller towns. In an arranged marriage too, only a girl is asked all kinds of questions. I really want this to change."
On the other hand, Kriti's alleged relationship with Sushant Singh Rajput has been grabbing headlines time and again. Recently while talking to a leading daily, here's what she had to say-
"Gone are the days when enjoying a movie or dinner with a co-star would be called a date. There is nothing wrong in being friends with your co-actors and if that involves dinners or movies, why not? It's sad if I stop socialising with a friend, just because people are cooking up stories. I am not answerable to any one. I would still hang out with my male friends and people can assume anything they like. As for Sushant, I don't have control over what people talk about us. I have already spoken enough about it."

Yemenis check the damage in the aftermath of a reported air strike by the Saudi-led coalition in the Yemeni capital Sana'a on March 8, 2018. AFP
The US Senate has teed up a vote on ending the US military involvement in the Saudi war on Yemen.
Spearheaded by Senators Bernie Sanders, Mike Lee and Chris Murphy, the resolution would not include the US alleged targeting of al-Qaeda elements in the impoverished country, Press TV reported.
Once the Senate reconvenes on Tuesday, the lawmakers could have up to four hours of debate; therefore, a vote is expected at approximately 4:15 pm.
If passed, the measure would require all US forces to leave the war-ravaged country within 30 days.
"You know it's a new precedent. ... I think a lot of members on our side are trying to figure out what a yes vote means and what a no vote means," Texas Republican Senator John Cornyn told The Hill.
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle have already voiced opposition for the US support for Riyadh, implicated in war crimes in the neighboring country, but it is still unclear whether the effort could garner enough votes.

In the Yemeni capital Sana'a, residents surveyed the damage on March 8, 2018, following a reported air strike by the Saudi-led coalition. Meanwhile, the U.S. Senate is poised to vote on ending American military involvement in the Saudi-led war in Yemen. Spearheaded by Senators Bernie Sanders, Mike Lee, and Chris Murphy, the resolution, as reported by Press TV, would not affect U.S. operations against alleged al-Qaeda elements within the impoverished nation. When the Senate reconvenes, lawmakers will have up to four hours of debate, with a vote expected around 4:15 p.m. If approved, the measure would mandate the withdrawal of all U.S. forces from the war-ravaged country within 30 days.

Senator John Cornyn, a Texas Republican, noted the unprecedented nature of the vote, telling The Hill that many members are weighing the implications of their decision. While lawmakers from both parties have increasingly criticized U.S. support for Riyadh—particularly over allegations of war crimes in Yemen—it remains uncertain whether the resolution will secure enough votes to pass.

BERLIN (AP) - Borussia Dortmund's ex-coach Thomas Tuchel has testified at the trial of a man accused of bombing the German soccer club's bus that the attack was partly responsible for his departure.
Defender Marc Bartra and a police officer were hurt in the April 11 attack as the bus left a Dortmund hotel for a Champions League match against Monaco. Dortmund played, and lost, the game a day later.
The dpa news agency reported Tuchel suggested Monday at suspect Sergei W.'s trial that the attack led to a disagreement with chief executive Hans-Joachim Watzke over rescheduling the game, probably because "I was sitting in the bus and he wasn't."
Tuchel says it was a mistake to schedule the match a day later.
Tuchel was fired in May after an inconsistent season.
rewrite:
On Monday, March 19, 2018, former Borussia Dortmund coach Thomas Tuchel arrived at a German state court in Dortmund as both a witness and a figure deeply affected by the proceedings. The trial centers on Sergej W.—his surname withheld under German privacy laws—who stands accused of detonating three bombs targeting the Dortmund team bus in April of the previous year. Tuchel later provided testimony, revealing that the attack contributed to his eventual departure from the club.

The bombing occurred on April 11 as the team bus departed a hotel for a Champions League match against Monaco, injuring defender Marc Bartra and a police officer. The match was rescheduled and played a day later, a decision Tuchel publicly criticized during the trial. According to reports from the dpa news agency, Tuchel suggested the attack sparked a disagreement with club CEO Hans-Joachim Watzke over the rescheduling, remarking that the disparity in their perspectives likely stemmed from the fact that "I was sitting in the bus and he wasn’t." Tuchel maintained that playing so soon after the incident was a mistake.

Tuchel, who was dismissed in May following an inconsistent season, framed the bombing and its aftermath as a pivotal fracture in his relationship with the club’s leadership.

A COMMUNITY day has been arranged to spread awareness of a disability benefit campaign.
The free event, which will be held at Set The Bar next to Wrexham Bus Station, will take place from 1pm to 11pm tomorrow in aid of the Save The Welsh Independent Living Campaign (SWILG).
There will be a number of performances throughout the day including Wrexham One World Community Choir, Luke Gallagher, Jamie Hamilton and more.
Disability campaigner Nathan Lee Davies is encouraging residents to turn out and support the event, which is expected to draw visitors from all over North Wales.
He said: “SWILG is an absolutely vital movement and a campaign that must be won.
“I implore people to come along to our completely free community day and I would encourage everyone to get involved with us on this SWILG campaign.
“We currently have a fantastic exhibition on in Theatre Clwyd, Mold, which we are proud to have put together.
“People such as the film-maker Ken Loach, to performers like Attila The Stockbroker, to some English and Welsh MPs and AMs, to Welsh Labour Grassroots/
Momentum to the local Labour parties in Clwyd South and Wrexham have given their full, official support.
“I cannot tell you how much that means to me and thousands like me.
“As I say, this is a campaign we simply cannot afford to lose.”
The Welsh Government became responsible for supporting those who had been receiving Independent Living Fund payments after the UK government closed the scheme in June 2015.
According to the charity Disability Rights UK, Welsh Independent Living Grant funding will continue during 2017-2018, but local councils will meet with the people receiving them to discuss the replacement support they need – by March 31, 2019, all recipients will receive their support from local councils.
To find out more about the campaign, search for @SaveWILG on Facebook.
For more information about the community day, search for the event 'Save the Welsh Independent Living Grant (SWILG) Community Day' on Facebook.

Aussie Rules: The Gympie Cats' clash against Bundaberg's Across the Waves last weekend resulted in the Cats disputing the final score.
After singing the club song, thinking they had secured a hard fought victory, the Cats were told they had lost the game by two points.
Cats officials recorded Gympie 12.12 (84) and Across the Waves 12.8 (80).
The goal umpires recorded Across the Waves 12.8 (80) and Cats 11.12 (78).
Cats coach and co-captain Courtney Findlay said the Cats were in the process of disputing the final score.
"We believe we kicked three goals in the final quarter but the goal umpires only recorded two,” he said.
"The papers have been lodged to AFL Queensland with proof backing up our belief. Hopefully we hear back this week.”
Gympie welcomed back Madry Tonkin who was sidelined due to a suspension from last year.
"Despite playing his first game of the season, Tonkin played well,” Findlay said.
"He was rotated through a few different positions and he handled it well.”
Cats' Jack Cross had another stand out performance, backing up from last week's game.
"He played up forward and was quiet creative,” Findlay said. "Jack won contested possessions in the midfield and when the game was to be won, he kicked a crucial goal.” Cross and Tonkin were not the only stand out Cats players; Jesse Lawrence had a great game in the midfield.
Cats head back to Bundaberg this Saturday to play Brothers Bulldogs at 3pm at Brothers AFL complex.
rewrite:
In a dramatic turn of events, the Gympie Cats are challenging the official result of their recent Aussie Rules match against Bundaberg’s Across the Waves. After celebrating what they believed was a hard-fought victory, the team was informed they had actually lost by two points. Club officials recorded a final score of Gympie 12.12 (84) to Across the Waves 12.8 (80), while the goal umpires’ official tally had Across the Waves at 12.8 (80) and the Cats at 11.12 (78). According to Cats coach and co-captain Courtney Findlay, the discrepancy stems from the final quarter. “We believe we kicked three goals in the final quarter, but the goal umpires only recorded two,” he said. The club has lodged formal papers with AFL Queensland, including evidence to support their claim, and hopes to receive a response this week.

The match saw a strong return for Madry Tonkin, who was playing his first game of the season after serving a suspension from last year. “Despite playing his first game, Tonkin played well,” Findlay noted. “He was rotated through a few different positions and handled it well.” Another standout was Jack Cross, who built on last week’s form with a creative performance up forward. “Jack won contested possessions in the midfield and, when the game was on the line, he kicked a crucial goal,” said Findlay. Jesse Lawrence also impressed with a great game in the midfield.

The Cats now look ahead to their next fixture, heading back to Bundaberg this Saturday to face the Brothers Bulldogs at 3pm at the Brothers AFL complex.

A racist manspreader assaulted a woman on the subway because she asked him to give her a bit more room to sit down, police said Saturday.
The 34-year-old victim was seated inside a northbound E train on Tuesday at around 5: 10 pm when the man sat down, partially on top of her, police said.
When she asked him to move for a moment so she could readjust herself, he shouted: “Just because you’re African American, you think you can go on your Kanye West rant, you black b***h,” according to cops, who have released an image of the suspect.
Later, as the woman was preparing to exit the train, she bumped his bag, prompting him to spit on the back of her head, said police.
The matter escalated even further when both passengers left at the 7th Avenue stop in Manhattan. When she grabbed the man’s backpack to confront him, he punched her in the shoulder and spit in her face again, and then fled back onto the train, police said.
Police describe the man as white-Hispanic, in his 30s, and approximately 5-foot-9 and 150 pounds.

All 26 Labour MPs in the North East have signed a joint letter calling on the Government to increase transport funding in the region.
Their plea follows similar requests for extra funding to improve the A19 in our area as part of this paper's Safe A19 campaign.
Our campaign logo.
Among the signatories are Sunderland MPs Julie Elliott, Sharon Hodgson and Bridget Phillipson, South Tyneside MPs Stephen Hepburn and Emma Lewell-Buck, Easington MP Grahame Morris and Hartlepool MP Mike Hill.
Along with their party colleagues, they are highlighting what they see as the inequality between what is spent on transport in the North and London "with London receiving more than double the amount the North receives per head of the population".
The letter, addressed to the Secretary of State for Transport, Chris Grayling, demands to know what his department intends to do to address "the lack of investment in the North East’s transport systems".
It also asks for urgent steps to be taken to increase funding levels to address "ongoing chronic and historic underfunding in transport infrastructure across the North East of England."
Ian Mearns, MP for Gateshead, said: “the recent Institute for Public Policy Research report, Future Transport Investment in the North, with figures taken from official government statistics, graphically highlights the huge disparity in spending plans on transport infrastructure between the North East of England and London.
“It is widely recognised that there is no doubt that our transport infrastructure in the North East is, at best, poor and in many cases dreadful.
"Therefore, this is an urgent and unified appeal for government action to rectify a long-term problem.”
More than 2,000 people have already signed our campaign for an inquiry into the number of accidents on the A19 with more than 70 people suffering injuries last year in a stretch of dual carriageway from Wolviston, near Hartlepool, to Boldon.
The joint Sunderland Echo, Hartlepool Mail and Shields Gazette petition can be signed at Change.org by searching for Safe A19: A call for an inquiry into safety on the dual carriageway through the North East.

All 26 Labour Members of Parliament representing constituencies in the North East have united in a joint letter urging the Government to boost transport funding for the region. This appeal echoes ongoing calls, including those from this newspaper’s Safe A19 campaign, for additional investment to improve the A19 corridor.

The signatories include Sunderland MPs Julie Elliott, Sharon Hodgson, and Bridget Phillipson; South Tyneside MPs Stephen Hepburn and Emma Lewell-Buck; Easington MP Grahame Morris; and Hartlepool MP Mike Hill. Together with their regional colleagues, they underscore a perceived inequality in transport spending between the North and London, noting that "London receives more than double the amount the North receives per head of the population."

Addressed to the Transport Secretary, Chris Grayling, the letter presses his department to outline plans for tackling "the lack of investment in the North East’s transport systems." It further calls for immediate action to raise funding levels and remedy what it terms "ongoing chronic and historic underfunding in transport infrastructure across the North East of England."

Gateshead MP Ian Mearns emphasized the urgency, stating: “The recent Institute for Public Policy Research report, *Future Transport Investment in the North*, which draws on official government statistics, graphically highlights the huge disparity in spending plans on transport infrastructure between the North East of England and London. It is widely recognised that our transport infrastructure in the North East is, at best, poor and in many cases dreadful. Therefore, this is an urgent and unified appeal for government action to rectify a long-term problem.”

In a related effort, more than 2,000 people have already endorsed our campaign petition for an inquiry into safety on the A19. Last year alone, over 70 people were injured on the dual carriageway stretch between Wolviston, near Hartlepool, and Boldon. The joint petition by the Sunderland Echo, Hartlepool Mail, and Shields Gazette—titled *Safe A19: A call for an inquiry into safety on the dual carriageway through the North East*—can be signed on Change.org.

SEATTLE (AP) – Landlords will not be allowed to screen tenants based on their criminal records under a measure passed by the Seattle City Council.
The ordinance unanimously approved Monday says landlords can’t screen a tenant based on arrests or convictions. Landlords also won’t be able to ask about or consider arrests that didn’t lead to a conviction. The law won’t apply to adult sex offenders.
Supporters say the rise in online criminal background checks have made it harder for formerly incarcerated people to find housing and get back on their feet.
Councilwoman Lisa Herbold, a bill co-sponsor, says landlords can still screen tenants based on other factors, such as employment, credit scores and income ratios.
The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposed the measure, calling it poor policy with unintended consequences. The group says a mandate offering no supportive services won’t encourage landlords to take chances on under-qualified applicants.
rewrite:
SEATTLE (AP) – The Seattle City Council has passed a measure prohibiting landlords from screening potential tenants based on their criminal history. Approved unanimously on Monday, the ordinance bars landlords from considering arrests or convictions during the tenant selection process. This includes inquiries into arrests that did not result in a conviction. However, the law does not apply to registered adult sex offenders.

Proponents argue that the widespread use of online background checks has created significant barriers to housing for people with past convictions, hindering their reintegration into society. Councilwoman Lisa Herbold, a co-sponsor of the bill, notes that landlords may still evaluate applicants using other criteria, like employment status, credit history, and income.

The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposed the ordinance, labeling it a flawed policy with potential unintended outcomes. The association contends that a mandate without accompanying support services will not incentivize landlords to accept applicants they deem higher-risk.

WOODMERE, N.Y. (CBSNewYork) — A Far Rockaway man is facing criminal charges, accused of posing as a police officer at a Long Island synagogue.
Congregants heading for prayer services inside the Young Israel of Woodmere Temple are still disgusted by one visitor’s attempt Saturday to portray himself as law enforcement.
“He tried being a cop, impersonating a police officer,” Macis Rand of Nassau County said.
Rand says some congregants inside the Temple knew the man who tried to portray himself as a police officer. Rand is particularly angry it happened on the Sabbath.
“When I heard the news, that’s pretty crazy doing it to a schul, I don’t know what he was hoping to gain from it,” Rand said.
Temple security staff says 28-year-old Mikhail Mikhaylov first parked in an unauthorized spot then walked in wearing an NYPD baseball cap with handcuffs, mace, and a gold badge.
The head of security told police “I heard him say he was a cop but did not see his ID.”
When asked for ID, Mikhaylov allegedly said “you mean my shield?”
Mikhaylov then reportedly told security his ID was in his car before going to the parking lot and racing away.
Security wrote down his license plate number and arrested him at his home the next day.
One neighbor says it’s part of a disturbing trend.
“It particularly happens in the law enforcement area because a lot of people ride around pretending to be cops because they want to be somebody they’re not,” neighbor Pete Wagner said.
Congregants say Mikhaylov said he had a gun and two knives in the car, but he’s facing no charges for that. His legal aid attorney says he simply went to the temple to pray.
Temple leaders did not comment on whether Mikhaylov is a congregation member.

WOODMERE, N.Y. (CBSNewYork) — A man from Far Rockaway is facing criminal charges after allegedly impersonating a police officer at a Long Island synagogue this past Saturday. Congregants arriving for prayer services at the Young Israel of Woodmere Temple remain disturbed by the incident.

“He tried being a cop, impersonating a police officer,” said Macis Rand of Nassau County. Rand, who noted that some inside the temple recognized the man, expressed particular outrage that it occurred on the Sabbath. “When I heard the news, that’s pretty crazy doing it to a schul. I don’t know what he was hoping to gain from it,” he added.

According to temple security, 28-year-old Mikhail Mikhaylov first parked in an unauthorized spot before entering the building wearing an NYPD baseball cap and carrying handcuffs, mace, and a gold badge. The head of security informed police, “I heard him say he was a cop but did not see his ID.” When security asked for identification, Mikhaylov allegedly responded, “You mean my shield?” He then claimed his ID was in his car, proceeded to the parking lot, and sped away.

Security personnel recorded his license plate number, leading to his arrest at home the following day. Some in the community see the event as part of a worrying pattern. “It particularly happens in the law enforcement area because a lot of people ride around pretending to be cops because they want to be somebody they’re not,” neighbor Pete Wagner observed.

While congregants reported that Mikhaylov claimed to have a gun and two knives in his vehicle, he faces no related charges. His legal aid attorney stated that Mikhaylov had simply gone to the temple to pray. Temple leaders declined to comment on whether he is a member of the congregation.

Mikhaylov is now charged with criminal impersonation in the second degree and is being held on a $2,500 bond.

THE CANADIAN PRESS
HALIFAX -- Professors and support staff at the Nova Scotia Community College have agreed to new six-year collective agreements.
The Nova Scotia Teachers Union, which represents the two bargaining units, says a vote on management's final offer was held Tuesday.
Faculty members voted 55 per cent in favour of the offer, while 64 per cent of voters with the professional support bargaining unit were in favour.
The union says the agreements, which run from Sept. 1, 2014 to Aug. 31, 2020, were ratified following the vote and include a seven-per-cent wage increase over the six-year terms.
Under legislation, the employer is required to freeze the years of service used to calculate an employee's retirement service award as of March 31, 2015.
However, the union says under both agreements employees can either choose to collect their service award based on their salary at retirement, or collect it immediately based on their salary as of March 31, 2018.

Legislation requires the employer to freeze the years of service used to calculate retirement service awards as of March 31, 2015. However, under the new agreements, employees have a choice: they can either collect their service award based on their salary at retirement, or receive it immediately based on their salary as of March 31, 2018.

Residential developers get floor-area bonuses for including “affordable” apartments and for providing certain public amenities such as plazas — so why not also for arts and cultural facilities?
That’s a proposal by Charles S. Cohen, who just reopened the modernized Quad Cinema on West 13th Street to widespread cheers. As a major landlord who’s also an active film producer and distributor, he’s interested in bringing art-house movie venues, live theater and dance and related activities to neighborhoods lacking them.
Noting that arts institutions are “hard-pressed to find space” due to the same cost pressures that have driven out many small stores and restaurants, Cohen proposes zoning changes to allow residential developers to build more apartments — in exchange for making arts space available for free in the same building.
He said the situation is so dire that, “Lots of art cinemas around the country are resorting to a nonprofit form of operating, having to rely on personal donations from those who want to support them.”
So, he suggests, “Why not have the Department of City Planning incentivize creation of cultural amenities in areas where there’s demand for them?” He said that while the Planning Department would set the basic zoning framework, the Department of Cultural Affairs could be involved in vetting specific arts uses at a given location.
rewrite:
Residential developers already receive floor-area bonuses for including affordable apartments and providing public amenities like plazas. So why not extend similar incentives to arts and cultural facilities? This is the proposal put forward by Charles S. Cohen, a major landlord and active film producer who recently reopened the modernized Quad Cinema on West 13th Street to widespread acclaim. Cohen is keen to bring art-house cinemas, live theater, dance spaces, and related cultural activities to neighborhoods that lack them.

He points out that arts institutions are increasingly "hard-pressed to find space," squeezed by the same rising costs that have displaced many small shops and restaurants. To address this, Cohen suggests zoning changes that would allow residential developers to build additional apartments in exchange for dedicating space within the same building to arts organizations, free of charge.

The situation has grown so dire, he notes, that "lots of art cinemas around the country are resorting to a nonprofit model, relying on personal donations from supporters." In response, he asks, "Why not have the Department of City Planning incentivize the creation of cultural amenities in areas where there's demand for them?" While the Planning Department would establish the overall zoning framework, Cohen suggests the Department of Cultural Affairs could help vet specific arts uses for each location.

SYDNEY (AP) — A period of personal reflection in a South African jungle has convinced Australian tennis player Bernard Tomic that he's ready to return to the court.
Tomic quit the reality television show "I'm A Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here!" after only three days, saying that was long enough to reflect and realize "how I played last year and where I should be."
He said his short time in the jungle was his first break from his "fast-paced" lifestyle and gave was "a wake-up call."
"After being there for a couple days, it made me depressed and it made me a bit sad and I didn't want to continue doing that to myself," Tomic told News Corp Australia. "I need to get back on the court.
"I just started recently to get back and feeling good. I won a couple of matches at the Australian Open in the (qualifiers). I just regret leaving that last month-and-a-half behind. It wasn't the right thing for me to do."
But Tomic's comeback may depend on his ability to repair his relationship with Tennis Australia and national Davis Cup captain Lleyton Hewitt.
Hewitt has indicated Tomic's Davis Cup career may be at an end after he rebuffed several attempts to draw him back into the fold and said in an interview that Australia couldn't win the Davis Cup without him. Asked if Tomic would play for Austalia again, Hewitt said "it's highly doubtful."
"He's made some mistakes. It will be a long way back," Hewitt said. "He's digging a big hole for himself that he may never get out of."

He described his short jungle experience as his first real pause from a "fast-paced" lifestyle, serving as "a wake-up call." "After being there for a couple days, it made me depressed and a bit sad, and I didn't want to continue doing that to myself," Tomic told News Corp Australia. "I need to get back on the court. I've recently started training again and am feeling good. I won a couple of matches in the Australian Open qualifiers. I just regret wasting that last month-and-a-half. It wasn't the right thing for me to do."

However, Tomic's potential comeback may hinge on mending his strained relationship with Tennis Australia and national Davis Cup captain Lleyton Hewitt. Hewitt has suggested Tomic's Davis Cup career is likely over, citing the player's rejection of several outreach attempts and his claim in an interview that Australia could not win the Davis Cup without him. When asked if Tomic would represent Australia again, Hewitt responded, "it's highly doubtful."

"He's made some mistakes. It will be a long way back," Hewitt said. "He's digging a big hole for himself that he may never get out of."
