In Ngong township, Kenya, armyworms have been observed consuming maize leaves, as captured in file photographs. One such image from May 9, 1999, shows the pests attacking a maize garden. Separately, a 2017 file photo from South Africa’s Limpopo province depicts a crop-eating armyworm on a sorghum plant.

Authorities in Addis Ababa reported on Thursday that fall armyworms, a type of crop-devouring caterpillar, have now damaged harvests across southern Ethiopia. This marks the latest outbreak in a region already grappling with severe drought and widespread hunger. The invasion follows confirmed attacks in Uganda during March, where the pests affected farms in approximately 20 districts. Neighboring Kenya has also responded to reports of their presence by deploying a team of scientists and experts to investigate.

Ethiopia’s Ministry of Agriculture stated that the worms have infested nearly 10,700 hectares of farmland in the Oromiya area and the Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples’ (SNNP) region. Zebdios Selato, the ministry’s director for plant healthcare, said, “Thirty-five thousand liters of chemicals have been purchased and distributed to spray affected areas with insecticide.”

The infestation threatens to further reduce agricultural output in Ethiopia, where drought has already left 5.6 million people in need of food assistance. Across the wider region, drought and conflict have placed four countries—northeast Nigeria, Somalia, South Sudan, and Yemen—at risk of mass starvation, according to the U.N. refugee agency.

Originally native to the Americas, the fall armyworm has rapidly spread to multiple African nations, including Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, South Africa, Namibia, Mozambique, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The United Nations warns that the pest could reach Asia and the Mediterranean within the next few years.

WHITE BEAR LAKE, Minn. — Prosecutors say a Minnesota man lived in his house with the decomposing bodies of his mother and twin brother for about a year.
Sixty-year-old Robert James Kuefler of White Bear Lake is charged with interference with a dead body or scene of death because he neglected to tell authorities they died of natural causes, according to the St. Paul Pioneer Press .
The bodies were found last year. Kuefler was charged this week. Police say he told them his mother, 94-year-old Evelyn Kuefler, died in August 2015 and his brother, Richard Kuefler, died before that and he couldn’t bring himself to bury them.
The complaint says his mother’s body was decayed and skeletal and his brother’s body was “mummified.”
Robert Kuefler didn’t return a message left by The Associated Press.
——
Information from: St. Paul Pioneer Press, http://www.twincities.com
rewrite: In White Bear Lake, Minnesota, prosecutors allege that a man lived for roughly a year in his home alongside the decomposing remains of his mother and twin brother. Robert James Kuefler, 60, faces a charge of interfering with a dead body or death scene. According to the St. Paul Pioneer Press, he failed to report that both had died of natural causes. The bodies were discovered last year, though charges were only filed this week. Police state Kuefler told them his 94-year-old mother, Evelyn, died in August 2015, and his brother, Richard, had passed away even earlier. He claimed he could not bring himself to arrange burials. A court complaint describes his mother’s body as decayed to skeletal remains and his brother’s as “mummified.” Robert Kuefler could not be reached for comment by The Associated Press.

A number of Peace and Sport's champions have been in attendance at the 2017 Friendship Games in Bujumbura in Burundi.
The event, which brings together 200 children from Burundi, Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, is held in cooperation with the National Olympic Committee of Burundi and International Federations from nine sports.
This includes the respective worldwide governing bodies in athletics, basketball, boxing, volleyball, table tennis, baseball/softball, karate and taekwondo.
According to organisers, the Friendship Games in the Great African Lakes region are held to "promote better inter-cultural dialogue and to endorse the power of sport for change".
France's Pascal Gentil, a double Olympic bronze medallist in taekwondo, is among the Peace and Sport champions in attendance, along with compatriot Jean-Baptiste Alaize.
Paralympian Alaize recently won a bronze medal at the World Para Athletics Championships in London.
Jean-François Tordo, a retired French rugby union player who made 18 appearances for France, offered his technical expertise through Peace and Sport's "Sport Simple" initiative.
The Friendship Games in the Great African Lakes region are held to "promote better inter-cultural dialogue and to endorse the power of sport for change" ©Peace and Sport
The scheme "sees sporting practice areas, equipment and rules adapted to resources and environment and aims to promote a 'sport for all' approach", according to Peace and Sport.
"It is amazing to come here and see so many children enjoying sport and using it as a tool for dialogue and sharing," said Gentil.
"I cannot wait to get started tomorrow and see so many happy faces.
"I have been privileged to have achieved much in my sporting career and I feel it is my duty to give something back to the world.
"That is why it is important for me to be involved in events like this and act as a Peace and Sport champion for peace around the world.
"Paris 2024 shares these values of togetherness, friendship and unity with Peace and Sport and it is great to be here on behalf of the team.
"We hope to infuse these themes throughout the Games and use sport to change the world for the better."
The 2015 Friendship Games in Rwanda were initially due to be held in August before they were switched to November amid security concerns.
rewrite:
The 2017 Friendship Games in Bujumbura, Burundi, welcomed several champions from the organization Peace and Sport. Organized in cooperation with the National Olympic Committee of Burundi and nine International Federations, the event brought together 200 children from Burundi, Rwanda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The participating sports—each represented by their global governing bodies—included athletics, basketball, boxing, volleyball, table tennis, baseball/softball, karate, and taekwondo. As stated by the organizers, the goal of the Friendship Games in the Great African Lakes region is to "promote better inter-cultural dialogue and to endorse the power of sport for change."

Among the attending Peace and Sport champions was France’s Pascal Gentil, a double Olympic bronze medalist in taekwondo. He was joined by compatriot Jean-Baptiste Alaize, a Paralympian who recently earned a bronze medal at the World Para Athletics Championships in London. Additionally, Jean-François Tordo, a retired French rugby union player with 18 caps for his national team, contributed his technical expertise through Peace and Sport’s "Sport Simple" initiative. This program adapts sporting areas, equipment, and rules to local resources and environments, aiming to foster a inclusive "sport for all" approach.

Reflecting on the event, Gentil shared, "It is amazing to come here and see so many children enjoying sport and using it as a tool for dialogue and sharing. I cannot wait to get started tomorrow and see so many happy faces." He emphasized his personal motivation, stating, "I have been privileged to have achieved much in my sporting career and I feel it is my duty to give something back to the world. That is why it is important for me to be involved in events like this and act as a Peace and Sport champion for peace around the world." Gentil also drew a connection to the upcoming Olympic Games, noting, "Paris 2024 shares these values of togetherness, friendship and unity with Peace and Sport and it is great to be here on behalf of the team. We hope to infuse these themes throughout the Games and use sport to change the world for the better."

The Friendship Games have seen adjustments in the past due to practical challenges; for instance, the 2015 edition in Rwanda was originally scheduled for August but was moved to November that year because of security concerns.

The second Monday in October is Alaska’s first official Indigenous Peoples' Day, once celebrated as Columbus Day. The Bethel Cultural Center will be celebrating the first peoples of the YK Delta at 6 p.m. on Monday, October 9. The Kuskokwim Campus, along with all University of Alaska Fairbanks rural campuses, have planned a day packed with activities.
KuC Director Mary Pete says that the public portion of events will start at 6 p.m.
“With a welcome and blessing by AVCP President Vivian Korthuis and John McIntyre, who is a renowned artist and drummer,” said Pete.
Bethel Regional High School and other Lower Kuskokwim School District athletes are also planning Native Youth Olympic demonstrations.
“The KuC Yuyruk class, the Yup’ik dance class, is going to perform as well as a group of Chevak students. We have quite a number of Chevak students here this year,” said Pete.
Pete says that they look forward to celebrating the Day annually on campus.
The bill recognizing the second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples' Day was passed by the Alaska Legislature and signed into law this past June by Governor Bill Walker. Representative Zach Fansler is also looking forward to attending the event, as he was the first co-sponsor of the bill.
Refreshments will be served and the doors will open at 6 p.m. on Monday at the Cultural Center.
rewrite:
This October marks a historic shift, as the second Monday of the month is now officially recognized statewide as Indigenous Peoples' Day, replacing the former Columbus Day. In Bethel, the community will gather to honor the first peoples of the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta with a celebration at the Bethel Cultural Center, beginning at 6 p.m. on Monday, October 9. The Kuskokwim Campus, alongside all University of Alaska Fairbanks rural campuses, has organized a full day of activities.

The public event will commence at 6 p.m. with a welcome and blessing from AVCP President Vivian Korthuis and renowned artist and drummer John McIntyre, as noted by KuC Director Mary Pete. The evening will feature cultural performances, including the KuC Yuyruk (Yup’ik dance) class and a group of students from Chevak. Additionally, athletes from Bethel Regional High School and the Lower Kuskokwim School District will present Native Youth Olympic demonstrations.

Pete expressed enthusiasm for establishing this celebration as an annual campus tradition. The holiday was formalized when legislation, first co-sponsored by Representative Zach Fansler, was passed by the Alaska Legislature and signed into law by Governor Bill Walker this past June. Representative Fansler plans to attend the event. The celebration at the Cultural Center, with doors opening at 6 p.m., will include refreshments for all attendees.

ISTANBUL Turkish state-run lender Halkbank's operations and transactions fully comply with national and international regulations, it said in a statement regarding the arrest of its deputy general manager Mehmet Hakan Atilla in the United States.
Atilla was charged on Tuesday with participating in a multi-year scheme to violate sanctions against Iran and conspiring with Turkish-Iranian gold trader Reza Zarrab, who is already on trial in a case which has caused tensions between Turkey and the United States.
In a statement released to the Istanbul stock exchange late on Thursday, Halkbank (HALKB.IS) said there was news in some media organs in recent days discrediting the bank and misleading the public and investors regarding his arrest.
"Our Bank's operations and transactions fully comply with national and international regulations all the time. Our Bank takes all measures to protect its shareholders, business partners and depositors' rights," the statement said.
Turkey's foreign and justice ministers on Thursday described the arrest of Atilla as a "political" move. President Tayyip Erdogan has said he believed U.S. authorities had "ulterior motives" in prosecuting Zarrab, who was arrested in March 2016 in Miami.
Shares of Halkbank, Turkey's fifth-largest listed bank by assets, endured their biggest one-day fall on Wednesday, falling 14 percent after news of the arrest emerged.
Atilla is accused of conspiring with Zarrab to conduct hundreds of millions of dollars of illegal transactions through U.S. banks on behalf of Iran's government and other entities in that country.
"Our Bank has not intermediated any transaction in which any prohibited party or person or goods or services have been involved," Halkbank said in the statement, which was also published on the back page of Turkish newspapers on Friday.
It said the U.S. financial system and currency have not been used for such transactions related to trade with the country mentioned in the allegations.
(Writing by Daren Butler)
rewrite:
In a statement addressing the arrest of its deputy general manager, Mehmet Hakan Atilla, in the United States, Turkey’s state-run Halkbank asserted that all of its operations and transactions consistently adhere to both national and international regulations. Atilla was charged on Tuesday with involvement in a multi-year scheme to evade sanctions against Iran, allegedly conspiring with Turkish-Iranian gold trader Reza Zarrab, whose ongoing trial has strained relations between Turkey and the U.S.

The bank, in a filing to the Istanbul stock exchange late Thursday, responded to recent media reports that it said were discrediting the institution and misleading the public and investors. "Our Bank’s operations and transactions fully comply with national and international regulations at all times. Our Bank takes every measure to protect the rights of its shareholders, business partners, and depositors," the statement read.

Turkish Foreign Minister Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu and Justice Minister Abdulhamit Gül characterized Atilla’s arrest as a "political" action on Thursday. President Tayyip Erdoğan has previously expressed his belief that U.S. authorities hold "ulterior motives" in the case against Zarrab, who was arrested in Miami in March 2016.

Following news of the arrest, shares of Halkbank—Turkey’s fifth-largest listed bank by assets—plunged 14 percent on Wednesday, marking their steepest one-day decline. Atilla stands accused of conspiring with Zarrab to funnel hundreds of millions of dollars in illegal transactions through U.S. banks on behalf of Iran’s government and related entities.

Halkbank further clarified in its statement, which also appeared on the back pages of Turkish newspapers Friday, that it "has not facilitated any transaction involving prohibited parties, individuals, goods, or services." The bank added that the U.S. financial system and its currency were not used for any such transactions related to trade with the country referenced in the allegations.

WAILUKU, Hawaii — Less than a week after it opened, Maui’s first state-licensed medical marijuana dispensary is reworking its opening hours as demand for its product outstrips supply because of a backlog.
Maui Grown Therapies says it had expected its most recent batch of flowers to clear state lab certification by Saturday, but that didn’t happen, The Maui News reported. Company officials said it sold out its first batch of certified flowers Saturday.
Maui Grown Therapies opened for business Tuesday. Company officials say the dispensary could only sell flowers — resulting in depleted flower stocks on Maui and “disappointed patients.”
The company said it needs the Department of Health’s State Labs Division “to help unclog a backlog of products so Maui patients can have access to quality-assured medicinal cannabis products.”
It will be closed Monday and Tuesday and reopen at noon Wednesday, when it will sell to patients who make appointments through its website.
“It’s unfortunate that an administrative hindrance of this magnitude prevents patients from getting the help they need,” said Christopher Cole, director of product management for Maui Grown Therapies. “We had planned to open with a full range of derivative products such as concentrates, oils, capsules and topical products, but at the eleventh hour we discovered that the State Labs Division had failed to certify a lab to conduct testing of manufactured products.”
State offices were closed Saturday, and state Health Department officials could not be reached for comment.
“We could serve thousands of patients with the amount of manufactured product we currently have available for final compliance testing,” Cole said. “Even though we were approved by the Department of Health on May 24 to manufacture cannabis products, the restrictions placed on the state’s only licensed lab have prevented us from offering these products to our patients — and it is entirely unclear to us when this will change.”
The dispensary’s initial posted hours were 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Saturday. Dispensary hours have been changed to noon to 6 p.m. until further notice.
rewrite:
WAILUKU, Hawaii — Maui’s first state-licensed medical marijuana dispensary is adjusting its operations less than a week after opening, as overwhelming demand quickly depletes its limited supply amid a regulatory backlog.

Maui Grown Therapies, which opened this past Tuesday, had anticipated its latest batch of cannabis flowers would receive state lab certification by Saturday, but the clearance did not come through in time. According to The Maui News, the dispensary sold out its initial certified flower supply on Saturday. Because the business is currently permitted to sell only flowers—and not other derivative products—its available stock has run low, leaving many patients without access.

“It’s unfortunate that an administrative hindrance of this magnitude prevents patients from getting the help they need,” said Christopher Cole, the company’s director of product management. He explained that the dispensary had planned to open with a full range of items, including concentrates, oils, capsules, and topical products. However, at the last minute, they learned the State Labs Division had not yet certified a laboratory to test manufactured cannabis goods.

The company is urging the Department of Health’s State Labs Division to help clear the testing backlog so patients can obtain quality-assured medicinal products. “We could serve thousands of patients with the amount of manufactured product we currently have available for final compliance testing,” Cole noted. He added that although the business was approved to manufacture cannabis products back on May 24, restrictions on the state’s sole licensed lab have stalled the process indefinitely. “It is entirely unclear to us when this will change,” he said.

With state offices closed over the weekend, health department officials could not be reached for comment. In response to the supply shortage, Maui Grown Therapies will be closed Monday and Tuesday, reopening at noon on Wednesday by appointment only. The dispensary’s original hours—10 a.m. to 7 p.m., Monday through Saturday—have been scaled back to noon to 6 p.m. until further notice.

FORT LEE, N.J. (AP) — The Fort Lee Film Commission in New Jersey celebrated Black History Month by honoring a pioneering African-American filmmaker with ties to the area.
The Record reports (http://bit.ly/2l7a4Yd) that film and history enthusiasts gathered at the Fort Lee Museum to highlight the works of director Oscar Micheaux on Tuesday night. The film commission has honored the director annually since the group's inception in 2002.
The group discussed Micheaux's opposition of hate groups and his positive portrayals of African-Americans throughout the event.
Micheaux produced and directed five films in Fort Lee between 1920 and 1948. He is also credited with making the first African-American-produced sound film with an entirely black cast.
Fort Lee Film Commission Executive Director Tom Meyers says the group would like to expand the event to discuss more black filmmakers with an entire exhibit.
___
Information from: The Record (Woodland Park, N.J.), http://www.northjersey.com
rewrite:
In Fort Lee, New Jersey, the local Film Commission marked Black History Month by paying tribute to a groundbreaking African-American filmmaker with connections to the region. According to The Record, film and history buffs assembled at the Fort Lee Museum on Tuesday evening to spotlight the legacy of director Oscar Micheaux. Since its founding in 2002, the commission has recognized Micheaux each year.

Throughout the gathering, participants explored Micheaux’s resistance to hate groups and his affirming depictions of African-American life. Between 1920 and 1948, Micheaux produced and directed five films in Fort Lee. He is also noted for creating the first African-American-produced sound film featuring an all-black cast.

Tom Meyers, Executive Director of the Fort Lee Film Commission, expressed hope to broaden the event in the future, potentially developing a full exhibit dedicated to more black filmmakers.

CINCINNATI -- People are sharing a disturbing video of apparent child pornography on Facebook, saying they want the perpetrator to be found.
Police say that's exactly the wrong thing to do.
Several people sent the video to Scripps station WCPO in Cincinnati, which appears to depict an underage girl performing oral sex on an adult man. Many of the messages included the phrase "I want this to go viral." There's no indication where or when it was recorded, or who's in it.
Law enforcement agencies from Alabama to France have gotten complaints as the video continues to spread, AL.com reported. According to the Buffalo (New York) Police Department, "Facebook is aware of this and is working with authorities."
Police in Memphis, Tennessee, even warned that sharing the video "is considered distribution and you could be criminally charged for doing so.
"We understand that sharing information sometimes brings a criminal to justice, but sharing amongst Facebook friends is not the way to do it," the department said.
Aside from being graphic and possibly illegal -- the female's age isn't clear, though she seems to be a child -- police worry the video could carry some kind of malicious code meant to infiltrate a viewer's computer.
"Don't open it, don't share it, don't forward it," Cincinnati Police Lt. Steve Saunders said.
Instead, notify Facebook and then delete the video from your account.
Tony Garrett, executive director of Central Alabama Crime Stoppers, told AL.com "some things point to" the video being made in Alabama. But there's no confirmation of that.
rewrite:
CINCINNATI — A disturbing video circulating on Facebook, which appears to depict child pornography, is being shared by users who say they want the perpetrator identified. However, police warn that sharing the video is precisely the wrong response.

Several individuals sent the video to Scripps station WCPO in Cincinnati. The footage seems to show an underage girl performing a sex act on an adult man. Many of those sharing it included messages like “I want this to go viral.” The origins of the video—including where and when it was recorded or who is involved—remain unknown.

According to AL.com, law enforcement agencies from Alabama to France have received complaints as the video spreads. The Buffalo Police Department in New York stated that Facebook is aware of the situation and cooperating with authorities.

Police in Memphis, Tennessee, emphasized that sharing the video may constitute distribution of child pornography, which could lead to criminal charges. “We understand that sharing information sometimes brings a criminal to justice, but sharing amongst Facebook friends is not the way to do it,” the department said.

Beyond its graphic and likely illegal content—the girl appears to be a minor, though her exact age is unclear—authorities also fear the video could contain malicious software designed to infect viewers’ devices.

Cincinnati Police Lt. Steve Saunders urged the public: “Don’t open it, don’t share it, don’t forward it.” Instead, he advised users to report the content directly to Facebook and then delete it from their accounts.

Tony Garrett, executive director of Central Alabama Crime Stoppers, told AL.com that certain details suggest the video may have been produced in Alabama, though this has not been confirmed.

(Agencia CMA Latam) - Argentinean state-owned oil company YPF, in association with Petronas E&P Argentina (PEPASA), plans to move ahead with a project in the La Amarga Chica area, in the Province of Neuquén, in the Vaca Muerta field.
The joint investment commitment in this third stage, expected to be concluded in 2018's third quarter, amounts to US$ 192.5 million.
For this third and final stage in La Amarga Chica, both companies contemplate the drilling of ten horizontal wells and the construction of new works and facilities to transport the shale oil produced in the area. After the completion of this last stage, the companies will be able to decide on the start of the full development of the area.
by Agencia CMA Latam

Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Ross Cockrell is getting ready to enter his third season with the Steelers and his second straight season the team’s full-time starter. He also started seven games in 2015. But according to coach Mike Tomlin, he is still looking for development in all areas for the young cornerback.
Coach Tomlin addresses the media following day 2️⃣ of minicamp. https://t.co/O9KXfy9Nqm — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) June 14, 2017
I think we forget sometimes that Cockrell is only 25 years old. He spent one season with the Buffalo Bills before coming to the Steelers, but he’s still very young. He got tossed into a starting role back in 2015 essentially by default but has done well in his trial by fire.
Part of why Tomlin and the Steelers are counting on development from Cockrell is that the team is making something of a transition to more man coverage this season which will require him to get better in all those areas to acclimate to the change.
The Steelers have loaded up at the cornerback position but Cockrell and Artie Burns seem to have the top two spots locked down. Cockrell definitely has the mentality to become a top man cornerback but needs to keep showing that development to the coaches.
rewrite:
Entering his third season with the Pittsburgh Steelers, cornerback Ross Cockrell is poised for his second consecutive year as a full-time starter, adding to the seven games he started back in 2015. However, head coach Mike Tomlin has emphasized that the young defender still needs to develop across all areas of his game.

As Tomlin noted to the media following minicamp, it’s easy to overlook that Cockrell is just 25 years old. After a brief stint with the Buffalo Bills, he was thrust into a starting role largely by necessity in 2015 and has handled that trial by fire commendably. Now, with the Steelers shifting toward more man coverage this season, Cockrell’s continued growth is essential to adapt to the new defensive scheme.

While Pittsburgh has bolstered its depth at cornerback, Cockrell and Artie Burns are projected to hold the top two spots. Cockrell possesses the mindset to excel as a premier man-coverage corner, but he must consistently demonstrate his progress to the coaching staff to fully realize that potential.

KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WATE) — Zoo Knoxville welcomed two new animals.
The zoo celebrated the hatching for two female Bali mynahs. The birds were hatched to the parents Zane and Kadek. The species is critically endangered.
The species has been driven to near-extinction due to unsustainable and illegal trapping to meet the demand of the pet trade, according to the zoo. There are only less than 100 Bali mynahs left in their native range in Indonesia.
“We are focusing on species that need our help to make a difference for the future of those populations,” said Michael Ogle, curator of ornithology and herpetology at Zoo Knoxville. “Every chick counts when you have a population as vulnerable as the Bali mynah and the two hatched here in Knoxville are part of a bigger safety net that accredited zoos are working to maintain.”

rewrite:
KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WATE) — Zoo Knoxville has announced the arrival of two new residents: a pair of recently hatched Bali mynah chicks. The zoo celebrated the hatching of these two female birds, born to parents named Zane and Kadek. This event is particularly significant because the Bali mynah is classified as a critically endangered species.

According to the zoo, the species has been pushed to the brink of extinction primarily due to unsustainable and illegal trapping for the pet trade. In their native range on the Indonesian island of Bali, fewer than 100 of these striking white birds are estimated to remain in the wild.

“We are focusing on species that need our help to make a difference for the future of those populations,” said Michael Ogle, curator of ornithology and herpetology at Zoo Knoxville. “Every chick counts when you have a population as vulnerable as the Bali mynah. The two hatched here in Knoxville are part of a bigger safety net that accredited zoos are working to maintain.”

The chicks, which hatched in late September, are part of a coordinated Species Survival Plan (SSP). This program, managed by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums, aims to ensure the genetic health and long-term survival of threatened and endangered species through carefully managed breeding programs across accredited institutions. The arrival of these two chicks represents a hopeful step in the collective effort to preserve a species that faces an extremely uncertain future in its natural habitat. Zoo Knoxville’s participation in this plan underscores the role modern zoos play in conservation, acting as arks for biodiversity and engaging in vital work that extends far beyond their own gates.

The government of Malawi has signed financing agreements aimed to enhance the Shire Valley Transformation Programme and Agriculture Commercialization Project in the country.
Speaking during the signing ceremony on Friday at the Ministry of Finance offices, Capital Hill in Lilongwe, World Bank country director for Tanzania, Malawi, Burundi and Somalia, Miss Bella Bird said their organization is committed to help boost various sectors of agriculture in African countries.
“Word Bank is passionate about increasing the diversity of products and financing in agricultural sectors in Africa including Malawi,” said Bird.
She added that, World Bank is focused to extend irrigation farming in order to raise productivity among small scale famers in Shire Valley.
According to Bird, the World Bank has budgeted USD160 million for the government of Malawi to help support Shire Valley transformation program and agricultural commercialization project.
“We have put a lot of money aside to be used for the two major projects and this is the latest project that World Bank has ever prepared in Malawi for the first time,” she explained.
She said 300 farming cooperatives in the country will benefit with the project noting that this would ease access to international markets by the farmers in the country. She further applauded the country’s leadership for introducing the two projects.
Speaking at the same event, the Minister of Finance, Economic Planning and Development, Goodall Gondwe thanked World Bank for helping the country in the transformation and commercialization projects.
“World Bank has done a great thing as the government of Malawi is working on transforming projects in different sectors in the country,” said Gondwe.
He said this would help bring more agricultural factories in the country which will subsequently help create more job opportunities for the youth.
He also said the factories would help add value to the agricultural produce throu the manufacture of cooking oil and peanut butter among others.
Gondwe urged the general public to join hands in order to bring the two programs to fruition.
rewrite:
The Malawian government has entered into new financing agreements designed to strengthen the Shire Valley Transformation Programme and the Agriculture Commercialization Project. The signing ceremony was held on Friday at the Ministry of Finance offices on Capital Hill in Lilongwe. During the event, World Bank Country Director for Tanzania, Malawi, Burundi, and Somalia, Bella Bird, emphasized her organization's dedication to supporting agricultural development across Africa.

“The World Bank is passionate about increasing both the diversity of products and the financing available within agricultural sectors in Africa, including here in Malawi,” stated Bird. She added that the Bank is particularly focused on expanding irrigation farming to raise productivity among small-scale farmers in the Shire Valley region. According to Bird, the World Bank has allocated USD 160 million to the Malawian government specifically for these two initiatives.

“We have set aside substantial funding for these major projects. This represents the latest and most comprehensive project the World Bank has prepared for Malawi to date,” she explained. Bird noted that approximately 300 farming cooperatives across the country are poised to benefit, which will in turn ease their access to international markets. She also commended Malawi's leadership for championing these programs.

Also speaking at the ceremony, Minister of Finance, Economic Planning and Development, Goodall Gondwe, expressed his gratitude to the World Bank for its support. “The World Bank has done a great thing, as our government is actively working to transform various sectors within the country,” said Gondwe.

He highlighted that the projects would help attract more agricultural processing factories to Malawi. This industrialization, he explained, would create significant job opportunities for the youth. Furthermore, these factories would add substantial value to local produce through the manufacture of goods like cooking oil and peanut butter. Minister Gondwe concluded by urging the public to join hands with the government to ensure the successful implementation of both programs, fostering greater economic growth and food security for the nation.

ANKARA The arrest of a senior Turkish banker by U.S. authorities will be discussed with U.S. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson when he visits Ankara this week, Turkey's foreign minister said on Wednesday.
In an interview with broadcaster TRT Haber, Foreign Minister Mevlut Cavusoglu also called for a transparent process regarding Hakan Atilla's arrest, and said the Turkish consul general was unable to receive information about Atilla until a formal statement was made.
U.S. prosecutors on Tuesday charged Mehmet Hakan Atilla, a deputy general manager at state lender Halkbank (HALKB.IS), with participating in a multi-year scheme to violate U.S. sanctions against Iran, escalating a case that has added to tensions between the United States and Turkey.
Shares in Halkbank slumped as much as 16 percent on Wednesday.
(Reporting by Daren Butler and Humeyra Pamuk; Writing by Ece Toksabay; Editing by David Dolan)
rewrite: ANKARA — Turkey's foreign minister stated on Wednesday that the arrest of a senior Turkish banker by U.S. authorities will be raised during U.S. Secretary of State Rex Tillerson's visit to Ankara this week. In an interview with broadcaster TRT Haber, Foreign Minister Mevlut Cavusoglu urged transparency in the case of Hakan Atilla, noting that the Turkish consul general could not obtain details until an official statement was issued. U.S. prosecutors charged Mehmet Hakan Atilla, a deputy general manager at state lender Halkbank (HALKB.IS), on Tuesday with involvement in a years-long scheme to evade U.S. sanctions against Iran. This case has heightened tensions between the two nations. Following the news, Halkbank shares fell by up to 16 percent on Wednesday.

Luton Foodbank has launched its ‘Christmas Appeal’ as the charity asks kind residents to help adults and children in poverty and crisis.
Luton Foodbank recently launched their own downloadable advent calendar, which asks for much-needed items to help generate donations over the 24 days leading up to Christmas.
Donations from residents are of crucial importance, as demand for food parcels rise again in Luton.
Project co-ordinator Salma Khan, said: “The idea is simple – one item placed in a bag each day of advent, to then be donated to Luton Foodbank.
“Donations from the public are a lifeline that ensure we are here for those in desperate need and the Foodbank uses local referral agencies to ensure that the food is directed to those who really need it.”
Launched in 2013, the charity provide emergency food supplies to local people in crisis and in poverty, working in partnership with local organisations.
Mick Dillon, CEO of Citizens Advice Luton, one of Luton Foodbank’s primary partners, claimed: “Every day we see the positive impact a food parcel can have, especially as more working families are struggling to manage against damaging benefit reformations, which must be paused.”
For more information about Luton Foodbank, a list of what to include in your calendar, volunteering opportunities and more, call: 01582 725838.
See the charity website www.lutonfoodbank.org.uk to download the calendar.
rewrite:
Luton Foodbank has launched its annual Christmas Appeal, calling on the generosity of local residents to support adults and children facing poverty and crisis. To make giving easier, the charity has introduced a downloadable advent calendar, suggesting a much-needed item for each of the 24 days leading up to Christmas. This initiative aims to steadily generate crucial donations during a period of rising demand for food parcels in the community.

Project coordinator Salma Khan explains, “The concept is simple: set aside one item each day of Advent, then donate the full bag to Luton Foodbank. Public contributions are our lifeline, enabling us to serve those in desperate need. We work with local referral agencies to ensure all food reaches the people who need it most.” Since its founding in 2013, the foodbank has provided emergency supplies to locals in crisis, operating in partnership with community organizations.

Mick Dillon, CEO of Citizens Advice Luton, a key partner, adds, “We witness daily the profound difference a food parcel makes. This is especially vital as more working families struggle due to damaging benefit reforms, which must be paused.” For further details—including a full list of requested items, volunteering opportunities, or to download the advent calendar—visit www.lutonfoodbank.org.uk or call 01582 725838.

TORONTO — The Canadian team behind the animated film "The Breadwinner" hopes Monday's Golden Globe nomination will shine a light on its timely subject matter and promote empathy.
The film stars the voice of Toronto actress Saara Chaudry as 11-year-old Parvana, who disguises herself as a boy in order to support her family while her father is wrongfully imprisoned by the Taliban in Afghanistan in 2001.
The film is a Canadian co-production and has a homegrown cast, about half of whom are Muslim and have Afghan heritage. Oscar-winning actor-director Angelina Jolie is an executive producer.
"Everyone keeps saying that this is a film that's come out at the right time because of what's going on, especially in the States, the Muslim ban, and I think this is a film that can actually help shed a light on what's going on around the world that we're not normally used to — especially that's a film for kids," Andrew Rosen, a Toronto producer on the film, said in a phone interview after the Golden Globe nominations were announced.
"We've had a lot of kids watch this and ask their parents and ask at Q-and-As, 'Is this real' or 'Did this happen 100 years ago?' And we have to say 'No, this is happening now.' I think it's really helpful when families go see it, for families to actually have this conversation with their kids."
"The Breadwinner," which was nominated for best animated film, is adapted from Canadian author Deborah Ellis's children's novel. The book is based on the testimony of Afghan women she spoke with in refugee camps in Pakistan.
Irish animator Nora Twomey directed and acclaimed Canadian composers Jeff Danna and Mychael Danna did the score for the film, which is open in several cities in Canada and the U.S.
Rosen and his Aircraft Pictures partner Anthony Leo have been working on the project since 2009.
The other co-producing countries are Ireland and Luxembourg.
"It's a film that shows the effects of war on ordinary people and we don't see that nearly enough, and I think it will help inform our decisions about whether or not we allow our governments to go to war," Ellis said Monday from her home in Simcoe, Ont.
rewrite:
TORONTO — Following a Golden Globe nomination for best animated film, the Canadian creators of "The Breadwinner" hope the recognition will draw broader attention to the film’s urgent themes and foster greater empathy among audiences.

The movie features Toronto actress Saara Chaudry as the voice of Parvana, an 11-year-old girl in Taliban-controlled Afghanistan in 2001. After her father is unjustly imprisoned, Parvana cuts her hair and poses as a boy to work and provide for her family. A Canadian co-production with Ireland and Luxembourg, the film boasts a largely homegrown cast—about half of whom are Muslim and have Afghan heritage—and counts Oscar-winner Angelina Jolie as an executive producer.

"For families, this film opens up a necessary conversation," said Toronto-based producer Andrew Rosen in a phone interview after the nominations were announced. "Many people have remarked on its timeliness, especially given current events like the Muslim ban in the United States. This story helps shed light on realities that are often distant from our daily lives, and it does so in a way that’s accessible for younger viewers."

Rosen noted that children who have seen the film often ask whether the events are real or historical. "We have to tell them, 'No, this is happening now.' That’s why it’s so valuable—it gives families a starting point to discuss difficult, ongoing issues in the world."

Adapted from Canadian author Deborah Ellis’s children’s novel, which was inspired by interviews with Afghan women in Pakistani refugee camps, "The Breadwinner" was directed by Irish animator Nora Twomey and scored by acclaimed Canadian composers Jeff Danna and Mychael Danna. Rosen and his Aircraft Pictures partner Anthony Leo have been developing the project since 2009.

Ellis, speaking from her home in Simcoe, Ontario, emphasized the film’s wider relevance. "It portrays the impact of war on ordinary people, something we don’t see nearly enough," she said. "I believe it can help inform how we think about the decisions our governments make regarding conflict." Currently in limited release across Canadian and U.S. cities, the film aims to resonate not only as a compelling story but as a poignant reminder of human resilience amid adversity.

ZURICH, March 31 Switzerland's Office of the Attorney General (OAG) expressed frustration over the apparent decision by Dutch authorities not to inform it in advance about raids tied to suspected tax evasion, the OAG said on Friday.
"The Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland is disconcerted about the manner in which this has been organized with the conscious non-inclusion of Switzerland... The attorney general expects a written explanation from the relevant leading Dutch authorities and is examining further actions," the OAG said in an emailed statement.
Earlier, Dutch prosecutors said they had launched an international hunt for people seeking to hide assets and evade taxes after receiving a tip-off about undisclosed accounts at a Swiss bank.
Credit Suisse said separately that authorities looking into client tax matters had visited its offices in London, Paris and Amsterdam and it was cooperating with them.
(Reporting by Joshua Franklin, Editing by Michael Shields)
rewrite:
ZURICH, March 31 — Switzerland’s Office of the Attorney General (OAG) voiced frustration on Friday over Dutch authorities’ apparent failure to provide advance notice of raids related to suspected tax evasion. In an emailed statement, the OAG said it was “disconcerted about the manner in which this has been organized with the conscious non-inclusion of Switzerland.” The Swiss attorney general is seeking a written explanation from leading Dutch authorities and is considering further steps.

The statement follows an announcement by Dutch prosecutors, who said they had begun an international investigation into individuals suspected of hiding assets and evading taxes after receiving a tip about undisclosed accounts at a Swiss bank. Separately, Credit Suisse confirmed that authorities conducting a tax inquiry had visited its offices in London, Paris, and Amsterdam, adding that the bank is fully cooperating.

(Reporting by Joshua Franklin, Editing by Michael Shields)

BRUNSWICK COUNTY, NC (WWAY) — The Sergei Foundation is a North Carolina non-profit committed to saving the lives of family pets and is expanding to Brunswick and New Hanover counties.
Since being founded in Winston-Salem in 2009, the foundation has helped more than 600 families and raised thousands of dollars. It’s primary focus is to obtain critical veterinary care and to avoid unnecessary euthanasia or surrender of pets to shelters or rescues.
- Advertisement -
Founder Karen Fullerton says the group is a state-wide organization already, and is now ready to serve Brunswick and New Hanover Counties.
The Sergei Foundation’s programs are unique. Most other rescues or welfare non-profits do not provide funding for pet care once the animal has been adopted and labeled a “companion pet.” If they do it is minimal and does not typically cover diagnostics. The foundation fills these gaps so pets are not left to suffer inhumanely at home without treatment, are surrendered to over-crowded shelters, or are euthanized due to lacking finances.
If you would like to volunteer or need assistance, visit their website here, contact them on Facebook or email info@sergeifoundation.org
rewrite:
The Sergei Foundation, a North Carolina non-profit dedicated to saving family pets, is expanding its services into Brunswick and New Hanover counties. Founded in Winston-Salem in 2009, the organization has already assisted over 600 families and raised thousands of dollars statewide. Its primary mission is to provide critical veterinary care, preventing unnecessary euthanasia or the surrender of pets to shelters.

Founder Karen Fullerton notes that while the group already operates across the state, it is now poised to serve these coastal communities directly. What sets The Sergei Foundation apart is its unique approach. Unlike many other rescue or welfare non-profits, which typically cease funding once an animal is adopted as a "companion pet," this foundation steps in to cover ongoing care. Others may offer minimal support that often excludes diagnostics, leaving pets to suffer untreated at home, be surrendered to overcrowded shelters, or face euthanasia simply due to financial constraints. The foundation works to fill these critical gaps.

For those interested in volunteering or seeking assistance, more information is available on their website, through their Facebook page, or via email at info@sergeifoundation.org.

KINSTON, N.C. (WNCT) — Nearly 40 teachers went home with grant money Monday.
Members of the Lenoir County Education Foundation delivered the grants to the teachers.
36 teachers from 12 schools received checks for grant money totaling 15,500 dollars.
Laura Lee Sylvester, executive director of the Kinston-Lenoir County Chamber of Commerce, said it is a great honor to help make better education available.
“It’s an opportunity for businesses in Kinston and Lenoir County to help out schools and our teachers offer additional projects in educational programs for our kids,” said Sylvester.
Teacher Aaron Murdock plans to use his money to buy Legos to help kids better understand math.
“I’ve written several, but this is the first one I’ve actually won, so it’s a good feeling to know that now I’m going to be able to purchase the things that really help students to learn,” Murdock said.
Each recipient went home with a balloon and check in an envelop.

A total of 36 educators from 12 different schools were awarded grants summing to $15,500. Laura Lee Sylvester, executive director of the Kinston-Lenoir County Chamber of Commerce, expressed pride in the initiative, stating, “It’s an opportunity for businesses in Kinston and Lenoir County to help out schools and our teachers offer additional projects in educational programs for our kids.” One recipient, teacher Aaron Murdock, plans to use his grant to purchase Legos, aiming to help students grasp mathematical concepts more effectively. “This is the first grant I’ve actually won,” Murdock shared. “It’s a good feeling to know that now I’m going to be able to purchase the things that really help students to learn.” Each teacher left with a balloon and a check in an envelope.

Published: 16 April 2017
South Central Railway (SCR) division which is headquartered in Secunderabad, Telangana has reported Rs 3564 crore, passenger transport earnings for the financial year 2016-17. This is highest earnings in its history. The announced earnings are increased by Rs 252 crore compared to previous year, and the passengers are increased by 9.16 million. In previous year totally 366.6 million traveled where as in 2016-17 it is 375.8 million.SCR has released a press statement on its earnings in which it stated that 9 trains are newly introduced for passengers, 7 trains travel distance is increased and for one train frequency is increased. According to the statement it attached 40 coaches to regular trains thus increasing 2600 berths everyday. In 2016-17 the SCR had totally attached 14,741 coaches which provided about 6 lakhs berths on temporary basis to facilitate the passengers.Earnings from ticket checking is about Rs 125 crore and totally 1.69 lakh ticket-less travel cases are registered.To cope with summer holiday rush totally 400 trains and 2000 coaches have been arranged on temporary basis.
rewrite:
Published on April 16, 2017, the South Central Railway (SCR) division, headquartered in Secunderabad, Telangana, announced passenger transport earnings of ₹3,564 crore for the 2016-17 financial year. This marks the highest earnings in the division’s history, reflecting an increase of ₹252 crore over the previous year. Passenger numbers also rose by 9.16 million, from 366.6 million to 375.8 million.

In a press release detailing these results, SCR noted several service enhancements: nine new trains were introduced, the travel distance for seven existing trains was extended, and the frequency of one train was increased. Additionally, by attaching 40 coaches to regular services, the division added approximately 2,600 berths daily. Over the full year, SCR attached a total of 14,741 coaches on a temporary basis, creating around 600,000 extra berths to accommodate passengers.

The division also reported earnings of roughly ₹125 crore from ticket checking, with 169,000 cases of ticket-less travel registered. To manage the summer holiday rush, SCR arranged 400 special trains and 2,000 additional coaches temporarily.

PHILADELPHIA — B.J. Johnson scored 25 points and Amar Stukes added 20 and La Salle outlasted St. Joseph's for an 81-78 win on Saturday.
La Salle (10-13, 4-6 Atlantic 10) outscored the Hawks 13-7 in the last three minutes and Stukes put the Explorers up for good. Johnson and Pookie Powell made six free throws combined, and Taylor Funk and Shevar Newkirk each missed 3s for a chance to tie.
Right before halftime, following Pierfrancesco Oliva's 3, Johnson reeled off eight straight with a layup and two 3s in succession, Stukes added a layup and Powell made a pair of free throws and La Salle reduced its deficit to 41-38.
La Salle continued to chip away, tied it at 58 with Saul Phiri's two free throws and went up six with a pair of Jamir Moultrie 3s. Newkirk responded with back-to-back 3s to even it.
rewrite:
PHILADELPHIA — B.J. Johnson led with 25 points and Amar Stukes added 20 as La Salle edged St. Joseph's 81-78 on Saturday. The Explorers (10-13, 4-6 Atlantic 10) secured the win by outscoring the Hawks 13-7 in the final three minutes, with Stukes hitting the decisive shot. Johnson and Pookie Powell then combined for six clutch free throws, while Taylor Funk and Shevar Newkirk each missed potential tying three-pointers.

Just before halftime, after Pierfrancesco Oliva’s three-pointer, Johnson sparked a run with eight straight points on a layup and two consecutive threes. Stukes added a layup and Powell sank two free throws, cutting La Salle’s deficit to 41-38.

La Salle kept chipping away after the break, tying the game at 58 on Saul Phiri’s free throws and building a six-point lead behind a pair of Jamir Moultrie threes. Newkirk answered with back-to-back threes to knot the score again, setting up the tense finish.

MIAMI (CBSMiami) – A coach is facing charges after hitting a 5-year-old with a tennis racket, but he and his lawyer told CBS4 that’s not the whole truth.
Osmailer Torres’ attorney says his client accidentally struck the child during a tennis lesson all while trying to protect other pupils.
Because of that, the lawyer is asking the court to grant his client immunity.

The little boy is seen opening the door at the playground and making his way toward the instructor and other children.

The 31-year-old Torres was arrested in July of 2016 and charged with child abuse.
Torres’ lawyer says when questioned by detectives his client maintained his innocence explaining that if the child was hit it was accidental.
The lawyer released a statement that read, in part:

The healthy food blogger and former Miss NI contestant has had a blast in the kitchen whipping up the brunch of her dreams using avocados, sweet potatoes and eggs – just a few of the life-changing gifts that could benefit disadvantaged communities in some of the world’s poorest countries.

A 13-year-old schoolgirl amazingly survived this impact after an out-of-control livery cab struck her on a Brooklyn sidewalk Thursday.
Gitel Hershenbaum suffered only a fractured leg — and her dad credits her heavy backpack.
“The backpack was very full of books, and that’s what pulled her back” onto the hood of the car instead of being hurled airborne, Israel Hershenbaum told WABC’s “Eyewitness News.”
The incident happened at 8:15 a.m. at the corner of 18th Avenue and 55th Street in Borough Park.
The driver had apparently suffered a heart attack and lost control of the car, officials said.
Surveillance video shows Gitel standing on the sidewalk and suddenly spotting the black Toyota Camry — its open rear door flapping — as it barrels her way. She turns to run, but is struck from behind.
The 48-year-old driver was rushed to Maimonides Medical Center, where he was listed in critical condition.
He was not expected to be charged, officials said, because the crash was caused by a medical episode.

US oil production seen thwarting OPEC effort to boost prices Print | Front Page | Email this story To:
From:
Message:
From (email):
Message:
PARIS (AP) — OPEC's plan to cut production and support prices is likely to be undone by increased output in the U.S., the International Energy Agency predicted Wednesday.
If correct, that could keep a lid on oil and energy prices as a glut of supply grows despite the efforts of countries in the OPEC cartel and allies like Russia to limit production.
The IEA, a Paris-based body that advises oil-consuming states on energy matters, said in its monthly oil report it expects production in non-OPEC states like the U.S. to grow 700,000 barrels daily this year. It predicts that output will grow even faster next year, by 1.5 million barrels daily, "which is slightly more than the expected increase in global demand."
"Our first outlook for 2018 makes sobering reading for those producers looking to restrain supply," said the report.
OPEC and 10 other countries led by Russia agreed last week to extend for nine months, to March, a production cut of 1.8 million barrels a day initially agreed on in November. The move is meant to drain the market of excess supply.
The recovery in the price of oil from last year's lows has, however, made it profitable once again for U.S. shale oil companies to ramp up production.
The U.S. benchmark for crude was down 56 cents to $45.90 a barrel after the report's release.
rewrite:
VOL. 41 | NO. 23 | Friday, June 09, 2017

PARIS (AP) — The International Energy Agency predicted Wednesday that rising oil production in the United States is likely to undermine OPEC’s efforts to cut output and lift prices. If accurate, this surge in U.S. supply could prevent any significant increase in oil and energy costs, even as OPEC and allied producers like Russia work to limit their own production.

In its monthly report, the Paris-based IEA—which advises oil-consuming nations—forecast that non-OPEC production, led by the U.S., will grow by 700,000 barrels per day this year. The agency further projected output will climb even more sharply in 2018, by 1.5 million barrels daily, noting that this increase “is slightly more than the expected rise in global demand.” The report cautioned, “Our first outlook for 2018 makes sobering reading for those producers looking to restrain supply.”

Last week, OPEC and ten other countries, including Russia, agreed to extend an existing production cut of 1.8 million barrels per day for an additional nine months, through March 2018. The original agreement, reached in November, was intended to reduce a global oversupply of crude. However, the partial recovery in oil prices from last year’s lows has already encouraged U.S. shale producers to profitably ramp up drilling again.

Following the release of the IEA’s report, the U.S. benchmark price for crude fell 56 cents to $45.90 a barrel.

Thursday marked the deadline for cities to submit formal proposals to host Amazon’s second headquarters. New York, like dozens of others, put its bid forward, though some commentators argue the eventual “winner” of this corporate prize may end up the biggest loser in the long run.

In Queens, a different kind of display is making headlines. The Queens Museum now finds itself exhibiting its own disgrace, having reversed its decision to cancel a planned re-enactment event after facing intense public backlash.

Meanwhile, Governor Cuomo’s administration is taking a firm stance against the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement targeting Israel. New York has compiled a blacklist of foreign companies that support BDS, effectively boycotting the boycotters. This policy clash spilled into a tense City Hall hearing, where pro-Palestinian protesters repeatedly disrupted proceedings on a resolution condemning such boycotts, leading to dozens of ejections as accusations flew from both sides.

Amid growing international pressure, some observers note that Israel is forming unexpected alliances. While activists abroad mark “Israel Apartheid Week,” Israeli diplomats are engaging with governments once considered unlikely partners, a shift attributed in part to increasing Western hostility.

In Europe, the BDS movement has gained significant traction, making it the main battleground in what some describe as an economic war against Israel. In contrast, the movement in the United States remains largely confined to certain academic circles. There are calls for New York to leverage its economic influence to help curb the campaign’s spread in Europe.

Critics of BDS condemn the movement’s tactics and narratives, labeling them as fundamentally dishonest and harmful. This sentiment is echoed by voices with deep ties to progressive and academic communities, who reject the boycott as counterproductive and divisive.

Questions about underlying support for BDS have even reached the highest levels of U.S. politics. Despite public denials, President Obama has faced accusations of tacitly aiding the movement through certain policy positions, highlighting the deep domestic divisions on the issue.

Nevertheless, the boycott movement recently encountered notable setbacks. In London, the British government issued a stern warning that public authorities supporting boycotts against Israel could face severe penalties, signaling a significant political and legal challenge to BDS efforts abroad.

WASHINGTON (AP) — The latest developments in the U.S.-China trade dispute, including plans for reciprocal tariffs (all times local):

**4:15 a.m.**

German Chancellor Angela Merkel stated that the European Union will do everything possible to prevent a trade war with the United States, but emphasized that Washington must also contribute to that effort. The Trump administration has already imposed tariffs on EU steel and aluminum and is considering additional duties on automobiles, trucks, and auto parts.

Addressing the German parliament on Wednesday, Merkel said, "It is worth every effort to try to defuse this conflict so that it doesn’t turn into a real war, but of course there are two sides to that." She stressed that a well-functioning global economy relies on nations cooperating as partners.

**11:00 p.m.**

U.S. authorities have granted China's ZTE Corp. temporary permission to resume some business with American companies, providing limited relief from a ban imposed over the tech firm's exports to Iran and North Korea.

This week's order from the Commerce Department follows a settlement in which ZTE agreed to pay a $1 billion fine, replace its executive team, and hire U.S.-selected compliance officers. The authorization allows ZTE to conduct transactions necessary to maintain existing telecommunications networks and mobile phones, and to support security features, through August 1.

ZTE had suspended most operations since April, when it was barred from purchasing U.S. components and technology. Prior to the ban, the company was spending an estimated $1.8 billion annually with American suppliers.

Arsenal’s restaurant scores three stars for sustainability
The Diamond Club at Arsenal’s Emirates Stadium has scored three stars for green dining.
The Sustainable Restaurant Association (SRA) said it achieved the highest ‘Food Made Good’ rating – a first for a sports stadium restaurant – by demonstrating “outstanding levels” of sustainability across its operation.
It rates restaurants based on a wide range of sustainability and ethical practices, including the use of locally sourced meat and fish, waste reduction and energy efficiency policies.
The restaurant sources 75% of its food locally and has partnered with charities to reduce food waste by redistributing it to people in need.
Andrew Stephen, Chief Executive of the SRA said: “Luxury, football and sustainability are three words you don’t always associate together.
“But the team at the Diamond Club have married them together, matching their passion for serving ethically sourced ingredients with a commitment to ensure those ingredients help provide meals for people who need them rather than ending up in the bin. A winning combination.”

The Diamond Club restaurant at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium has earned a three-star sustainability rating from the Sustainable Restaurant Association (SRA), achieving the highest possible 'Food Made Good' score. This marks the first time a sports stadium restaurant has received this top honor. The SRA assesses venues on a broad spectrum of ethical and sustainable practices, such as sourcing local ingredients, minimizing waste, and improving energy efficiency. The Diamond Club sources 75% of its food locally and works with charity partners to redistribute surplus meals to those in need, drastically cutting food waste.

Andrew Stephen, CEO of the SRA, commented: "Luxury, football, and sustainability aren't always linked, but the team at the Diamond Club has brought them together seamlessly. They've paired their dedication to ethically sourced ingredients with a commitment to ensuring that food helps feed people, rather than going to waste. It's truly a winning combination."

A fire broke out on the sets of Akshay Kumar's film 'Kesari' at a village in Maharashtra's Satara district today, police said. The fire was brought under control, a Satara Police control room official told PTI. Nobody was hurt, he added.
The shooting for the film is taking place at Pimpode Budruk village in Wai teshsil, around 30 km from Satara, he said.
Asked how the fire started, police said the shoot had a scene depicting a bomb explosion and apparently some embers fell on set material in the vicinity.
The film's unit has been shooting there for the climax and final portions of the film with Akshay Kumar, who had left the spot for the day after completing the shoot, police said.
The film is being jointly produced by Dharma Productions, Cape of Good Films and Azure Entertainment.
There has been no word so far from either Akshay Kumar or the film makers about today's incident.
The film is a war drama inspired by the Battle of Saragarhi of 1897, where an army of 21 Sikhs fought against 10,000 Afghans. The film also stars Parineeti Chopra and is being directed by Anurag Singh.
Earlier also, the film was in the limelight when it was reported that Salman Khan refused to co-produce the film along with Karan Johar.
rewrite:
A fire erupted today on the set of Akshay Kumar's film 'Kesari' in a village within Maharashtra's Satara district, according to police. Officials confirmed the blaze has been contained and that no injuries were reported. The incident occurred in Pimpode Budruk village in Wai tehsil, approximately 30 kilometers from Satara, where shooting is currently underway.

Police indicated the fire originated during the filming of a scene depicting a bomb explosion, where stray embers are believed to have ignited nearby set materials. At the time, the unit was shooting climax and final sequences. Akshay Kumar, having finished his scenes for the day, had already left the location.

'Kesari' is a joint production by Dharma Productions, Cape of Good Films, and Azure Entertainment. As of now, neither Akshay Kumar nor the filmmakers have commented on the incident.

The film is a war drama based on the 1897 Battle of Saragarhi, in which 21 Sikh soldiers faced an army of 10,000 Afghans. It also stars Parineeti Chopra and is directed by Anurag Singh. Previously, the project garnered attention when reports surfaced that Salman Khan declined to co-produce the film with Karan Johar.

I am a single mom renting a condo in the Goleta Union School District. I have been a PTA member for eight years, ever since my first child started kindergarten. I am also a past PTA president and a past PTA treasurer, and have served in many other volunteer capacities at our school to raise the necessary funds to keep our educational specialists.
Also, I have served as a District Advisory Council member for our school, and was a member of the Goleta Union School District Strategic Task Force for several years, working directly with the school board and the district to ensure proper curriculum development. All of this is to say that I am very involved in our community, and I care deeply about the welfare of our children and future opportunities that we make available to them as they grow into adulthood.
I have been studying the issue of Bishop Ranch including the request that the Goleta City Council initiate an amendment to the city’s General Plan to change the zoning designation from agriculture, which according to the city’s own study isn’t a viable use for the property, to urban. This would allow the owner of the property to build much-needed workforce housing that would also generate substantial sums of money for our local school district. This seems like a win-win to me. It seems to me this property offers great potential for people like me who need more housing opportunities that are affordable.
I hope the Goleta City Council will vote to initiate Tuesday night and allow the property owner to create a master-planned community on a portion of this site for local families to live and raise their children.
Dawn Eyman
Goleta
rewrite:
As a single mother renting a condo within the Goleta Union School District, I have been deeply engaged in our schools and community for many years. My involvement began eight years ago when my oldest child entered kindergarten, and I joined the PTA. Since then, I have served not only as a PTA member but also as a past president and treasurer, along with numerous other volunteer roles—all focused on raising essential funds to retain our educational specialists.

Beyond the PTA, I have participated as a District Advisory Council member and served for several years on the Goleta Union School District Strategic Task Force. In that capacity, I worked directly with the school board and district leadership to support thoughtful curriculum development. This longstanding commitment reflects how much I care about our children’s well-being and the future opportunities we create for them as they grow.

Recently, I have been looking closely at the proposal regarding Bishop Ranch. The request before the Goleta City Council is to amend the city’s General Plan by redesignating the zoning from agricultural—which the city’s own studies show is not viable for this land—to urban. Such a change would enable the property owner to develop critically needed workforce housing, which would in turn generate significant ongoing revenue for our local school district. To me, this represents a clear win-win: it addresses the urgent demand for affordable housing while providing lasting benefits to our schools.

This property holds real promise for families like mine who are seeking attainable housing options in our community. I sincerely hope the City Council will vote to initiate the amendment process on Tuesday night, allowing the creation of a well-planned community on a portion of this site—a place where local families can thrive and raise their children.

Dawn Eyman  
Goleta

The Charge d'Affaires ad interim of Japan to Nepal, Shinya Machida, signed a grant contract to provide medical equipment to the Laborer Women and Child Welfare Council (LWCWC). The equipment will be installed in the Valley Health Center, located in Bhaktapur District.
The grant contract was signed between the Embassy of Japan and Mrs. Ranju Napit, Chairperson of the Health Center.
The Project for the Installation of Medical Equipment at the Community Health Center in Bhaktapur District is funded under the Grant Assistance for Grassroots Human Security Projects (GGP) of the Japanese Government. The grant assistance amounts to USD 82,514 (approximately NPR 8.5 million).
According to a press release issued by Embassy of Japan, the project will support the installation of cutting-edge equipment such as an ECG machine, hematology analyzer, a mobile X-ray machine, ultrasound machine, etc. for use in diagnosis.
The Valley Health Center, located in Byasi (Bhaktapur) has been offering medical services, mainly to women and children, free of charge since its establishment in 2008.
The health center offers free diagnosis, free delivery assistance in rural areas, and basic medicines, and focuses on maternal and child health. In addition, the doctors and nurses of the center regularly visit the surrounding communities to provide counselling and to raise awareness on basic health.
According to a staff member at the center, young women in rural areas still tend to hesitate about going to hospital for diagnosis due to medical costs. “Many people tend to think of going to a hospital only when they are very sick and consider regular check-ups a waste of money”, said Mrs. Napit, Chairman of the Valley Health Center.
The medical equipment which will be provided under the grant scheme can assist the center to offer a wider range of services, including accurate check-ups, diagnosis and prenatal care.
The Embassy of Japan hopes that this project will contribute towards enhancing the center’s medical services provided to women and children in the suburbs of Kathmandu.
rewrite:
Shinya Machida, the Chargé d'Affaires ad interim of Japan to Nepal, has signed a grant contract to provide medical equipment to the Laborer Women and Child Welfare Council (LWCWC) for installation at the Valley Health Center in Bhaktapur District. The agreement was formalized between the Embassy of Japan and Mrs. Ranju Napit, Chairperson of the Health Center.

This initiative, titled "The Project for the Installation of Medical Equipment at the Community Health Center in Bhaktapur District," is funded through the Japanese Government's Grant Assistance for Grassroots Human Security Projects (GGP), with a contribution of USD 82,514 (approximately NPR 8.5 million). According to a press release from the Embassy, the grant will support the installation of advanced diagnostic equipment, including an ECG machine, hematology analyzer, mobile X-ray machine, and ultrasound machine.

Established in 2008 in Byasi, Bhaktapur, the Valley Health Center has been providing free medical services, primarily to women and children. Its offerings include free diagnosis, delivery assistance in rural areas, basic medicines, and a strong focus on maternal and child health. Staff from the center also conduct regular community visits to offer health counseling and raise awareness.

Despite these services, a staff member notes that many young women in rural areas remain reluctant to seek hospital care due to costs. Mrs. Napit, Chairman of the center, observed, "Many people tend to think of going to a hospital only when they are very sick and consider regular check-ups a waste of money." The new equipment is expected to help overcome such barriers by enabling a broader range of services, including accurate check-ups, diagnosis, and prenatal care.

The Embassy of Japan hopes this project will enhance the quality and reach of medical services for women and children in the Kathmandu suburbs, supporting the center's mission to deliver accessible and comprehensive care.

Police are appealing for information after a 15-year-old boy was stabbed in the Tredworth area of Gloucester.

LANSING (AP) — Gov. Rick Snyder’s Marshall Plan for Talent has been granted $100 million in funding from the Michigan Senate.
Lawmakers voted 30-2 Wednesday to establish a talent investment fund within the state’s Higher Education Student Loan Authority for the upcoming fiscal year.
The money would be funneled into initiatives to promote talent development in Michigan, mainly through support for technical and skills-based learning and partnerships between businesses and schools.
The two-bill package now heads to the House, which last month dinged Snyder’s $100-million goal by 25 percent in its budget.
Snyder, a term-limited Republican, unveiled the plan earlier this year and has said it is his top priority during his final year of leading a state that has seen a steadily deflating talent pool since the Great Recession.

LANSING (AP) — The Michigan Senate has approved $100 million in funding for Gov. Rick Snyder’s Marshall Plan for Talent. In a 30-2 vote on Wednesday, lawmakers established a talent investment fund within the state’s Higher Education Student Loan Authority for the next fiscal year.

The funding will support initiatives aimed at developing talent in Michigan, primarily by promoting technical and skills-based education and fostering partnerships between businesses and schools.

The two-bill package now moves to the House, which last month reduced Snyder’s original $100 million request by 25 percent in its own budget proposal.

Snyder, a term-limited Republican, introduced the plan earlier this year, calling it his top priority in his final year as governor. He aims to address the state's steadily declining talent pool, a trend that has persisted since the Great Recession.

In a delightfully unexpected television crossover, the world of Colin Dexter’s beloved detective Endeavour Morse is set to intersect with the iconic ITV soap opera Crossroads. Yes, as surprising as it may seem, an upcoming episode of the prequel series Endeavour will feature a young Detective Sergeant Morse—played by Shaun Evans—checking into a motel in Kings Oak. For longtime TV viewers, that name will ring a bell: Kings Oak was the fictional Midlands setting of the long-running series Crossroads.

The clever reference appears just 31 seconds into the extended trailer for the show’s fifth season, and sources close to the production confirm the nod is entirely intentional. In the episode, Morse stays at the very same Crossroads Motel while investigating the murder of a young woman across the Midlands. Given that Endeavour is set in 1968, Morse probably won’t bump into Benny—the beloved beanie-wearing handyman played by Paul Henry, who didn’t join the soap until 1975. However, viewers tuning in on Sunday, February 18th might just spot classic Crossroads characters from the era, such as Meg, Jill, or the unforgettable cleaner Amy Turtle.

Originally published in February 2018, this news highlights a playful blend of television worlds. Endeavour’s fifth season continues to air on PBS Masterpiece, inviting audiences to enjoy these clever nods to British TV history.

The component on consumers expectations finished at 86.5, below the preliminary reading of 86.7 and unchanged from the February's final figure.
