Rogers Family(DALLAS) — A 100-year-old Dallas, Texas, runner continues to show the world that you are only as old as you feel.
This weekend, Orville Rogers won big at the 2018 USATF Masters Indoor Track and Field Championships in Landover, Maryland.
“How great it feels at the age of 100 to break five new world track records and to bring home the gold,” he told ABC News on Monday.
In the 100 to 104 age category, Rogers set new records in the 60-meter, 200-meter, 400-meter, 800-meter and 1,500-meter events. And, he did it with his family cheering him on every step of the way.
The former World War II veteran was a bomber pilot who later became a commercial pilot. Rogers started running at the age of 50 and began competing in track meets when he turned 90.
Rogers, also the author of “The Running Man,” said he trains every other day and runs three times a week.
Rogers, a widower, has four children, three of whom are still alive; 14 grandchildren; and 11 great-grandchildren.
“We’re a very close family,” he told ABC News. “We take family vacations every summer for 44 years now and we enjoy getting together anywhere.”
In November, Rogers led partygoers as they collectively ran 100 miles at White Rock Lake in Dallas in celebration of his birthday.
“I live life with a capital ‘L,'” he told ABC affiliate WFAA-TV in November.

rewrite:
DALLAS — Orville Rogers, a 100-year-old runner from Dallas, Texas, is proving that age truly is just a number. Over the weekend, he celebrated a remarkable victory at the 2018 USATF Masters Indoor Track and Field Championships in Landover, Maryland. “How great it feels at 100 to break five world records and bring home gold,” Rogers told ABC News on Monday.

Competing in the 100 to 104 age category, Rogers set new world records in the 60-meter, 200-meter, 400-meter, 800-meter, and 1,500-meter events—all with his family cheering him on. A former World War II bomber pilot who later flew commercially, Rogers didn’t start running until he was 50 and only began competing in track meets at 90. Now, he trains every other day and runs three times a week, balancing his athletic discipline with a rich family life.

A widower, Rogers has four children, three surviving, along with 14 grandchildren and 11 great-grandchildren. “We’re a very close family,” he said. “For 44 years we’ve taken summer vacations together, and we love any chance to gather.” Last November, to mark his centennial, he led a group at White Rock Lake in Dallas in collectively running 100 miles. As he told ABC affiliate WFAA-TV at the time, “I live life with a capital ‘L.’” Through running and family, Rogers continues to inspire, showing that passion and perseverance know no age.

The dozen owners of Lamborghini Venenos--an ultra-rare supercar that costs $4 million and up-- will be receiving some bad news via registered mail: Their Italian dream machines are being recalled.
The 12-cylinder, 750-horsepower models that Automobili Lamborghini SpA billed as a “street-legal racing car” are among about 5,900 Aventadors the carmaker will recall worldwide over risks that a fuel system fault could lead to fires, the company said Tuesday.
Included in the recall are the only three Venenos hardtops sold, which carried a price of about $4 million (3 million euros), plus another nine Veneno Roadsters, originally listed at $4.5 million.
About 1,500 Aventadors, which start at around $400,000, also are affected by the recall in the U.S., according to a recall notice posted on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s website Tuesday.
The ultra-rare Venenos have appreciated in value like works of art since they were built. Lamborghini said in 2013 that it would sell only three copies of the Veneno to customers for 3 million euros apiece, about $4 million at the time. Automobile Magazine reported in March 2016 that one was listed for sale for $11.1 million.
Over-Revving
In a statement, Lamborghini said faults in the Aventador’s evaporative emissions control system could cause fuel vapors to not be treated properly. Combined with "particular maneuvers" such as "engine over-revving at idle," fuel vapors could contact hot gasses and lead to a fire risk, "especially with a not approved aftermarket exhaust system."
With a full fuel tank, "certain driving conditions" could cause gasoline to come into contact with hot exhaust system components, according to NHTSA.
The company says it’s unaware of any driver or passenger injuries tied to the flaw, though a spokeswoman was unable to say whether any fires have been reported in the affected vehicles.
U.S. owners will be notified by registered mail and can schedule a service appointment at a Lamborghini dealer to upgrade the evaporative system, the company said.
rewrite:
Owners of the ultra-rare, multi-million-dollar Lamborghini Veneno are about to receive unwelcome news by registered mail: their Italian dream cars are being recalled. Automobili Lamborghini SpA announced Tuesday that it is recalling roughly 5,900 Aventador models worldwide due to a fuel system fault that could pose a fire risk. Among these are all twelve Venenos ever built—cars famously billed as "street-legal racing cars" with 12-cylinder engines producing 750 horsepower.

The recall includes the three original Veneno coupes, each sold for about $4 million (3 million euros), along with nine Veneno Roadsters, which originally carried a price tag of approximately $4.5 million. In the United States, about 1,500 Aventadors—models that start around $400,000—are also affected, according to a notice posted on the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) website.

Since their limited production, the Venenos have appreciated dramatically, much like works of art. Lamborghini initially stated in 2013 it would sell only three Venenos to customers. By March 2016, Automobile Magazine reported one was listed for sale at $11.1 million.

The issue stems from faults in the Aventador’s evaporative emissions control system, which may not properly treat fuel vapors. Lamborghini warns that, when combined with “particular maneuvers” like “engine over-revving at idle,” these vapors could contact hot gases and create a fire hazard—a risk heightened “especially with a not approved aftermarket exhaust system.” NHTSA adds that, with a full tank, “certain driving conditions” could allow gasoline to meet hot exhaust components.

The company states it is unaware of any injuries related to the flaw, though a spokeswoman could not confirm whether any fires have been reported in the affected vehicles. U.S. owners will be notified via registered mail and can schedule a service appointment at a Lamborghini dealer to upgrade the evaporative system.

To mark the occasion, Seven Sharp reporter and reformed smoker Mike Thorpe spoke to Dr Chris Atkinson, an associate professor of oncology at St George’s Cancer Care Centre in Christchurch, to help you kick the habit. "There is a time in every person who smokes' life where they sort of think, 'I don't need to do this, and that's when you need help,'" Dr Atkinson said. Smokers are four times more likely to kick the habit with the help of a healthcare professional, such as a family doctor, a pharmacist, or a helpline.
Dr Atkinson said it's hard to stop "because the addiction is complex".
"There's lots of different types of nicotine - there's lots of different influences that an addict has."
Smoking influences have lessened over the years as the Government tackles the habit, with cigarette ads being taken off the air, and tobacco sponsorship and smoking in bars being banned.
"I'd like to believe it [will happen] but by gosh, we've got a lot of work to do in the next seven years."
The percentage of smokers is currently at 16 per cent - a sharp decline from 33 per cent in 1983.
"700,000 Kiwis have given up and I think they've given up because the message is out there that it hurts people. Tobacco is hurting people."
rewrite:
To mark this occasion, Seven Sharp reporter and former smoker Mike Thorpe spoke with Dr. Chris Atkinson, an associate professor of oncology at St. George’s Cancer Care Centre in Christchurch, for advice on quitting. "Every smoker reaches a point where they think, 'I don’t need to do this anymore'—and that’s precisely when support is crucial," Dr. Atkinson noted. Statistics show that smokers are four times more likely to quit successfully with professional help, whether from a doctor, pharmacist, or a dedicated helpline.

Dr. Atkinson explained that quitting is difficult due to the complexity of addiction. "Nicotine dependence comes in many forms, and each smoker faces a unique set of influences," he said. Over the years, smoking’s social presence has diminished as the government has taken action, banning cigarette advertising, tobacco sponsorship, and smoking in bars.

While progress is evident—smoking rates have dropped sharply from 33% in 1983 to about 16% today—Dr. Atkinson remains cautiously optimistic. "I’d like to believe we can go further, but my goodness, we still have a lot to accomplish in the next seven years," he remarked. He attributes the positive trend to growing awareness: "Around 700,000 New Zealanders have quit, largely because the message is clear: tobacco harms people. That truth is making a difference."

On a party line vote the House passes a $4 trillion budget. It slashes social programs, repealing Obamacare and turning Medicaid into a pile of vouchers.
None of that is actually happening, though. Not yet, anyway.
The way Senate rules work, you need a two-thirds vote to block a filibuster. So as a practical matter who need a two-thirds vote to pass anything controversial.
But one exception is the budget. Budget bills require only a simple majority.
So Republicans want to use this loophole to pass changes to the tax code.
Instead of drafting a tax bill, they'll put the changes inside the budget. But in order to do that they need a budget to pot things inside.
The bill the House passed is the bill in which to insert tax code changes.
Nobody seems to expect the bill to pass the Senate in the form the House passed.
If you're on Medicaid you probably wonder if I can vouch for that.
I'm not a fan of vouchers.
And that's Crisis at a Glance.

rewrite:
In a party-line vote, the House has passed a $4 trillion budget plan that would deeply cut social programs, repeal the Affordable Care Act, and transform Medicaid into a system of vouchers. However, none of this is actually happening—at least not yet.

Under Senate rules, most controversial legislation requires a two-thirds majority to overcome a filibuster, making such measures difficult to pass. But there is a key exception: budget bills. These only need a simple majority to advance. Republicans intend to use this procedural shortcut to push through major changes to the tax code. Rather than drafting a standalone tax bill, they plan to insert those changes into the budget itself—which is why they first needed a budget framework to modify.

The version the House just passed is meant to serve as that vehicle. Yet few expect it to clear the Senate in its current form. If you rely on Medicaid, you might be worried about the shift to vouchers—a proposal I personally do not support. And that’s the crisis, at a glance.

SAN DIEGO (KGTV) - Point Loma neighbors are rallying to save a beloved bike track - a track they've built with their own hands, but no permits. The track on Famosa and Nimitz Boulevards was threatened on Monday.
“I rushed over here as quick as I could,” Darren Miller said. “I stood in front of the tractor and said, “I’m sorry I can't let you keep doing this.”
It’s still unclear who sent the bobcat to level the track. But - the land belongs to the San Diego Housing Commission.
Miller is a parent of two boys and says he started building the track last March after coming across the empty land. He added the jumps and curves, thinking it would become a sort of secret playground.
“I thought myself and a couple of other dads involved would have a small little track that or six or seven kids knew about. I had no idea that this many people loved it,” he said.
Monday night several families showed up for a rally to save the park, expressing their affinity for the neighborhood track.
“This is the most awesome-est place in the world,” eight-year-old Jude Hudson said, “So much fun because there are some bumps and curves.”
Parents agree.
“We don’t want this to go. This a good place to be and to exercise and to keep them off their phones." Jon Erb said. "You got parents that come out here on a daily basis, so you got chaperones down here and keeps them away from drugs.”
When 10News asked what the deal with the empty land was, the San Diego Housing Commission sent the following statement:
“An unauthorized and unpermitted makeshift bike park was set up by unknown individuals on the undeveloped property that is owned by the San Diego Housing Commission (SDHC) at the corner of Famosa and Nimitz Boulevard.
Some of the no trespassing signs placed on the property by SDHC have been removed. Without sufficient insurance, SDHC, a public agency, cannot allow the property to be used as a bike park.
The property is being planned to be developed as affordable housing. We are pleased to be working with the Community Planning Group on the future development of affordable housing at this site.”
rewrite:
SAN DIEGO (KGTV) — A community-built bike track in Point Loma, constructed without permits, is at the center of a neighborhood effort to preserve it. The track, located at the corner of Famosa and Nimitz Boulevards, faced demolition on Monday when heavy equipment arrived to level the site.

“I rushed over here as quick as I could,” said Darren Miller, a local parent. “I stood in front of the tractor and said, ‘I’m sorry, I can’t let you keep doing this.’” It remains unclear who ordered the equipment, but the land is owned by the San Diego Housing Commission.

Miller, a father of two, began building the track last March after noticing the vacant lot. He crafted jumps and curves, envisioning a hidden playground for neighborhood children. “I thought a few other dads and I would have a small track that maybe six or seven kids knew about,” he explained. “I had no idea this many people loved it.”

On Monday evening, dozens of families gathered at a rally to support the track, sharing their appreciation for the improvised park. “This is the most awesome place in the world,” said eight-year-old Jude Hudson. “It’s so much fun because there are bumps and curves.”

Parents echoed his enthusiasm. “We don’t want this to go. It’s a good place to exercise and keeps kids off their phones,” said Jon Erb. “Parents are out here daily, so there’s supervision. It keeps them active and away from negative influences.”

When contacted by 10News, the San Diego Housing Commission issued a statement clarifying its position: “An unauthorized and unpermitted makeshift bike park was set up by unknown individuals on undeveloped property owned by the San Diego Housing Commission at the corner of Famosa and Nimitz Boulevard. Some ‘no trespassing’ signs posted by SDHC have been removed. As a public agency, SDHC cannot allow the property to be used as a bike park without sufficient insurance. The site is planned for future affordable housing development, and we are working with the Community Planning Group on that process.”

For now, the track remains standing—a testament to community initiative, but its future hangs in the balance between neighborhood sentiment and official plans.

Despite lighter traffic with some schools having already broken up in town for Christmas, the major roads into the town centre were still clogged up as traffic took a cautious approach on icy roads.
The congestion effected buses, too, and The Harrogate Bus Company posted that some of its most popular services - our 1A, 1B and 1C buses - were experiencing delays.

Overnight temperatures locally tonight into Tuesday will drop to -2C and tomorrow will be another cold day, though, perhaps, a smidgen warmer than of late.

Harrogate shivered through its coldest morning of the winter today, with temperatures plunging to -5°C. Drivers and buses alike slowed to a crawl on the icy roads. Despite lighter traffic due to some schools closing for Christmas, major routes into the town centre were clogged as motorists proceeded with extreme caution. This congestion impacted bus services, with The Harrogate Bus Company reporting delays on its popular 1A, 1B, and 1C routes.

DETROIT (AP) - Kameron Chatman had 21 points with eight rebounds to lead all five Detroit Mercy starters in double-figure scoring in a 74-60 victory over IUPUI on Friday night.
Chatman, who had four assists and three steals, scored 12 points in the first half when Detroit took a 38-28 lead after shooting 52 percent and leading by as many at 18.

rewrite:
DETROIT (AP) — Kameron Chatman scored 21 points and grabbed eight rebounds Friday night, leading all five Detroit Mercy starters in double figures as the Titans defeated IUPUI 74-60. Chatman, who also contributed four assists and three steals, put up 12 points in the first half, helping Detroit build a 38-28 lead after shooting 52 percent and leading by as many as 18 points.

The Titans never trailed, hitting 8 of 19 three-point attempts. Roschon Prince and Josh McFolley each added 14 points, with McFolley accounting for four of the team’s 11 steals. OTTAWA — The Supreme Court of Canada says records detailing the abuse of former residential school students can eventually be destroyed.
The unanimous high court ruling today brings clarity to an issue that pitted the privacy of victims against the importance of documenting a dark chapter in Canada's relations with Indigenous Peoples.
Students provided accounts of physical, sexual and emotional abuse as part of an independent assessment process to provide compensation — a program that flowed from a major 2006 settlement agreement.
The Supreme Court upheld a lower court ruling that said the material should be destroyed after 15 years, though individuals could agree to have their stories preserved at the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation in Winnipeg.
The federal government unsuccessfully argued the documentary record must be fully preserved to ensure what happened at the residential schools is never forgotten.
It said federal laws governing access to information, privacy and archives provide the proper balance for safeguarding the records of historical value while protecting individual privacy and confidentiality.
The Canadian Press
rewrite:
OTTAWA — Canada's Supreme Court has ruled that records documenting the abuse suffered by former residential school students may ultimately be destroyed. The unanimous decision resolves a longstanding conflict between protecting victims' privacy and preserving a crucial historical record of a painful era in Canada’s treatment of Indigenous Peoples.

These accounts of physical, sexual, and emotional abuse were gathered through an independent assessment process established to provide compensation, stemming from a major 2006 settlement agreement. The court upheld a lower ruling that the documents should be destroyed after 15 years, while allowing individuals to consent to having their testimonies archived at Winnipeg’s National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation.

The federal government had argued unsuccessfully that the complete documentary record must be kept to ensure the atrocities of the residential school system are never forgotten. It maintained that existing laws on access to information, privacy, and archives strike an appropriate balance between preserving historically valuable records and safeguarding personal confidentiality.

WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. officials are blaming the North Korean government for a series of cyberattacks dating to 2009 against media, aerospace, financial sectors and infrastructure in the United States and around the world.
The FBI and the Department of Homeland Security issued a warning this week, saying the cyberattacks were carried out by actors within the North Korean government who are known as “Hidden Cobra.”
“DHS and FBI assess that Hidden Cobra actors will continue to use cyber operations to advance their government’s military and strategic objectives,” the alert said.
U.S. officials are distributing internet addresses to help networks defend against any attacks. The FBI said it has high confidence that the internet addresses are linked to systems infected with Hidden Cobra malware to further exploit networks. The cyberattacks targeted weaknesses in Microsoft Corp. operating systems and Adobe Systems Inc.’s Flash software, which were patched in January and June, respectively.
The joint alert was issued Tuesday, the same day that American student Otto Warmbier, who was released from serving a 15-year sentence in a North Korean prison for participating in alleged acts against the government, arrived in Cincinnati, Ohio.
The U.S. remains in a standoff with North Korea over its nuclear program. The U.S. has issued sanctions, but Pyongyang has not made any move to give up weapons that it says are a deterrent to any invasion. Thousands of U.S. troops are based in neighboring South Korea, and the Demilitarized Zone between the North and South is one of the most heavily fortified borders in the world.

rewrite:
WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. officials have attributed a long-running series of cyberattacks, stretching back to 2009, to the North Korean government. These attacks have targeted media, aerospace, financial, and infrastructure sectors both in the United States and globally.

This week, the FBI and the Department of Homeland Security issued a joint warning, identifying the perpetrators as North Korean government actors operating under the name “Hidden Cobra.” The alert stated, “DHS and FBI assess that Hidden Cobra actors will continue to use cyber operations to advance their government’s military and strategic objectives.” In response, officials are distributing specific internet addresses to help network defenders block potential attacks. The FBI expressed high confidence that these addresses are linked to systems compromised by Hidden Cobra malware, which exploits known vulnerabilities. The attacks notably targeted weaknesses in Microsoft and Adobe Flash software; these vulnerabilities were patched in January and June, respectively.

The warning was released on Tuesday, coinciding with the return to Cincinnati, Ohio, of American student Otto Warmbier. He had been released from North Korean custody after being imprisoned for alleged acts against the government.

This cyber alert unfolds against a backdrop of ongoing tension between the U.S. and North Korea over its nuclear ambitions. Despite U.S. sanctions, Pyongyang has shown no willingness to relinquish weapons it considers a deterrent against invasion. The region remains heavily militarized, with thousands of U.S. troops stationed in South Korea and the Demilitarized Zone standing as one of the world's most fortified borders.

2017 has been a banner year for cheap flights around the world. In fact, overall prices for long-haul flights fell by seven percent. That’s great if you want to fly to Europe for the first time or finally see Bangkok’s famed street markets.
Over the last year or two airlines like WOWair, Norwegian, and AirAsia have been offering insanely cheap one way flights over the Atlantic for as little as $89 one way. Of course, there’s a big caveat here. Those prices rarely include seat assignments, onboard food or drinks, checked luggage, or even carry on bags. Still, if you’re willing to ride hard and fast over the Atlantic, you can now get there for less than a hundred dollar bill.
Well, 2018 is likely going to be even better. British Airways and Air France are officially getting into the budget airlines game with crazy cheap flights around Europe and competitive long-haul fares between the continents.
Air France launched Joon on December 1st. Their new budget airline is aimed squarely at “hipster millennials” and tech-savvy travelers. They’re already offering flights around Europe for $46 each way from Orly in Paris. By spring, they’ll have flights from Europe to South America and the Indian Ocean (Seychelles) for about $250 each way with plans to tackle the Trans-Atlantic market to the USA by summer.
British Airway’s Level started up last summer and aims at a broader base. They’re targeting millennials, families, and weekend warriors onto their well-fitted flights. They’re already offering flights between Europe and New York, Montreal, Boston, Los Angeles, Oakland, and Buenos Aires for as low as $149 each way.
What these big carriers seem to have caught on to is that there’s more to budget travel than just flights between Europe and America. Both have added South America and Asia to their destinations, opening a whole new world of exploration for budget travelers. And with at least two new airlines throwing their hat in the budget airfare ring, there’s sure to be some interesting price wars on our travel horizons throughout 2018.

rewrite:
The year 2017 was a standout for affordable air travel worldwide, with overall long-haul flight prices dropping by seven percent. This made it an ideal time for first-time trips to Europe or that long-awaited visit to Bangkok's vibrant street markets.

In recent years, carriers like WOWair, Norwegian, and AirAsia have revolutionized transatlantic travel by offering astonishingly low one-way fares, sometimes as little as $89. However, there's a significant catch: these base prices typically exclude seat selection, onboard meals and beverages, checked luggage, and sometimes even carry-on bags. Yet for travelers willing to embrace a no-frills journey across the Atlantic, reaching another continent for under a hundred dollars became a new reality.

Looking ahead, 2018 promises to be even more exciting for budget-conscious flyers. Major legacy airlines are now entering the low-cost arena, with British Airways and Air France introducing competitive budget services for both European and long-haul routes.

Air France launched its new subsidiary, Joon, on December 1st, specifically targeting "hipster millennials" and tech-savvy travelers. The airline already offers European flights from Paris Orly for just $46 each way. By spring, Joon plans to expand with routes to South America and the Indian Ocean (including the Seychelles) for approximately $250 each way, with ambitions to enter the transatlantic market to the United States by summer.

British Airways' low-cost venture, Level, took flight last summer with a broader appeal, catering to millennials, families, and weekend travelers seeking well-equipped yet affordable flights. Level already provides service from Europe to destinations like New York, Montreal, Boston, Los Angeles, Oakland, and Buenos Aires, with fares starting as low as $149 each way.

What these established carriers have recognized is that the budget travel market extends far beyond Europe and America. By adding South American and Asian destinations to their networks, they are unlocking a new world of exploration for cost-aware travelers. With at least two major new players entering the competitive budget airline scene, 2018 is poised to bring dynamic price wars and even more enticing deals for globetrotters.

New prosecutor in trial for former Lake County coroner Rudd
hello
A new appellate court prosecutor has stepped in to take over the perjury trial of former Lake County Coroner Dr. Thomas Rudd.
Prosecutor Bernard Murray said he does not anticipate having to delay the trial against Rudd, which is scheduled Jan. 16. Judge Victoria Rossetti asked the two sides to return to court Jan. 11 for a hearing on pretrial motions.
Murray took over the case after former prosecutor Brian Towne, 49, was charged with 13 counts of official misconduct and four counts of misapplication of funds stemming from his tenure as state's attorney in LaSalle County. The charges state Towne used public funds for personal use.
Rudd, 70, of Lake Forest, faces five counts of perjury charging him with making false statements on nominating petitions filed prior to an unsuccessful re-election bid in 2016. He faces up to five years in prison if convicted, though probation also is possible.
Authorities say Rudd swore under oath he was present when voters signed his nominating petitions. Prosecutors said 15 to 20 signatures on the petitions turned out to be false.
Rudd remains free on $150,000 bail.
rewrite:
A new prosecutor has taken over the perjury trial of former Lake County Coroner Dr. Thomas Rudd. Appellate prosecutor Bernard Murray now leads the case, replacing former prosecutor Brian Towne. Towne, 49, was recently charged with 13 counts of official misconduct and four counts of misapplication of funds related to his time as LaSalle County state’s attorney, accused of using public money for personal expenses.

Murray stated he does not expect to delay the trial, which remains scheduled for January 16. Judge Victoria Rossetti has asked both sides to return to court on January 11 for a hearing on pretrial motions.

Rudd, 70, of Lake Forest, faces five perjury counts. The charges allege he made false statements on nominating petitions filed ahead of an unsuccessful 2016 re-election bid. Prosecutors claim Rudd swore under oath that he was present when voters signed, but 15 to 20 signatures were later found to be invalid. If convicted, he could face up to five years in prison, though probation is also an option. Rudd remains free on $150,000 bail.

Druze residents of Masada village in the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights at a Syria independence day rally on April 17, 2017 (AFP Photo/JALAA MAREY)
Masada (AFP) - Hundreds of Druze on the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights marched Monday for Syrian independence day, carrying portraits of President Bashar al-Assad and chanting anti-Israel slogans.
"God save Syria!" they shouted as they rallied in the town of Masada. "Down with the occupation!"
Israeli officials say there are about 20,000 Druze on the strategic plateau seized by the Jewish state from neighbouring Syria in the 1967 Six-Day War.
Israel subsequently annexed the 1,200 square kilometres (460 square miles) of territory in an action never recognised by the international community.
But the vast majority of Golan Druze have retained Syrian nationality.
The civil war which has ravaged their homeland for the past six years is reflected in local divisions, with Masada opponents of the Assad regime refusing to march behind his picture.
But both sides are united in their opposition to the Israeli occupation, residents told AFP.
"We retain our Syrian identity and follow the path of national resistance," said Nasser Ibrahim, one of the organisers of Monday's march.
"With the crisis in Syria, Israel has increased its measures on the Golan," said Assad opponent Ayman Abu Jabal, referring to what he called Israeli-ordered changes to the Golan school curriculum.
Israel and Syria are still officially in a state of war, but Israel says it has no wish to get involved in the fighting.
It does, however, carry out strikes against its Lebanese foe Hezbollah, which fights for Assad in Syria.
Last month, Israel struck what it said were Hezbollah targets in Syria, drawing Syrian anti-aircraft missile fire in the worst flare-up between the two governments since the Syrian civil war began in 2011.
rewrite:
Hundreds of Druze residents in the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights marched on Monday, marking Syrian Independence Day with portraits of President Bashar al-Assad and chants against Israel. The rally, held in the town of Masada, echoed with cries of "God save Syria!" and "Down with the occupation!" Israeli authorities estimate roughly 20,000 Druze live on the strategic plateau, which Israel captured from Syria during the 1967 Six-Day War and later annexed—a move never accepted internationally. Most Golan Druze have kept their Syrian citizenship.

The devastating six-year civil war in Syria has created divisions locally. In Masada, opponents of the Assad regime refused to carry his portrait during the march. Yet, despite these internal splits, residents told AFP that both sides remain united in their rejection of the Israeli occupation. "We retain our Syrian identity and follow the path of national resistance," said march organizer Nasser Ibrahim.

Assad opponent Ayman Abu Jabal noted, "With the crisis in Syria, Israel has increased its measures on the Golan," pointing to what he described as Israeli-imposed changes to the local school curriculum. Although Israel and Syria remain officially at war, Israel states it has no intention of intervening directly in Syria's conflict. However, it has conducted strikes in Syria targeting Hezbollah, its Lebanese adversary, which fights alongside Assad’s forces. Last month, Israeli attacks on what it said were Hezbollah positions triggered Syrian anti-aircraft fire, marking the most serious clash between the two since the Syrian war began in 2011.

Bernie Sanders has just proven once and for all how biased he truly is against Christians. He proved that once again recently when he violated a Constitutional mandate that you are not allowed to apply a religious test when running for office.

VICTORIA - British Columbia's Liberal leadership race is expected to expand to eight candidates, with former transportation minister Todd Stone poised to enter the contest.
The Kamloops-South Thompson member of the legislature has scheduled three campaign-style events Tuesday stopping in Surrey, Victoria and finishing the day with an event at Thompson Rivers University in his hometown of Kamloops.
An email from former Liberal cabinet minister Peter Fassbender says B.C. needs a fresh vision to keep the province on track and Stone will make a special announcement about the Liberals party's future.
Stone released a YouTube video in September saying he was considering whether to run, then added that if he were to be leader, the B.C. Liberal Party would not accept the taxpayer subsidies that are being proposed by the minority New Democrats.
Former Surrey mayor Dianne Watts announced her intentions for the party's top job last month, along with 38-year-old Terrace businesswoman Lucy Sager and five current provincial Liberal politicians, Sam Sullivan, Mike Bernier, Andrew Wilkinson, Mike de Jong and Michael Lee.
The first of six candidate debates is set for Oct. 15 in Surrey, with party members electing a new leader to replace former premier Christy Clark in early February.
rewrite:
VICTORIA — The race for the leadership of British Columbia’s Liberal Party is likely to grow to eight candidates, as former transportation minister Todd Stone prepares to join the contest. Stone, the member of the legislature for Kamloops-South Thompson, has arranged three campaign-style events for Tuesday, with stops in Surrey and Victoria before concluding the day at Thompson Rivers University in his hometown of Kamloops.

In an email, former Liberal cabinet minister Peter Fassbender stated that British Columbia requires a renewed vision to stay on course and indicated that Stone will make a special announcement regarding the party’s future. Stone had previously signaled his interest in a YouTube video released in September, noting that if he became leader, the B.C. Liberal Party would reject proposed taxpayer subsidies put forward by the minority New Democrat government.

The field already includes former Surrey mayor Dianne Watts, who declared her candidacy last month, alongside Terrace businesswoman Lucy Sager and five sitting Liberal MLAs: Sam Sullivan, Mike Bernier, Andrew Wilkinson, Mike de Jong, and Michael Lee. The first of six scheduled debates will take place on October 15 in Surrey, with party members set to choose a new leader in early February, succeeding former premier Christy Clark.

Welcome to today's Aston Villa live blog for Thursday, June 15.

The Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday halted the Quezon City government from implementing a resolution that increases the city’s real property tax rates from 100 percent to 500 percent.
During an en banc session in Baguio City, the high court issued a temporary restraining order halting the implementation of Ordinance No. 2556 (Series of 2016).
The Alliance of Quezon City Homeowners’ Association questioned the ordinance that adjusts the fair market value of lands, houses and other structures.
Named respondents were Quezon City Mayor Herbert Bautista, the City Assessor’s Office and City Treasurer’s Office.
The SC ordered the Quezon City government to file its comment within 10 days from the receipt of the order.
Mayor Herbert Bautista welcomed the court’s ruling but he urged the SC to resolve the case “the soonest possible time.”
“We have yet to receive an official copy of the decision but the Quezon City government welcomes the development. We pray that the SC will resolve the matter the soonest possible time to ensure the smooth operations of the delivery of basic services to its constituents,” he said.
In a separate statement, the city’s Public Affairs’ office said that the city was “compelled” to adjust the fair market values of real properties after the Department of Finance and the Commission on Audit directed the city government to implement the “long-delayed” adjustment as mandated by Section 219 of Republic Act 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. Jomar Canlas and Dempsey Reyes
rewrite:
On Tuesday, the Supreme Court issued an order preventing the Quezon City government from enforcing a resolution that raises real property tax rates by 100 to 500 percent. The high court, during an en banc session held in Baguio City, granted a temporary restraining order against the implementation of Ordinance No. 2556 (Series of 2016). This ordinance, which adjusts the fair market value of lands, houses, and other structures, had been challenged by the Alliance of Quezon City Homeowners’ Association. Named as respondents in the case were Quezon City Mayor Herbert Bautista, along with the City Assessor’s Office and the City Treasurer’s Office.

The Supreme Court directed the Quezon City government to submit its comment within ten days of receiving the order. Mayor Bautista welcomed the court’s decision but urged a swift resolution. “While we have yet to receive an official copy of the ruling, the Quezon City government views this development positively. We hope the Supreme Court will resolve the matter at the earliest possible time to ensure the uninterrupted delivery of basic services to our constituents,” he stated.

Separately, the city’s Public Affairs Office explained that the adjustment was undertaken because the city felt “compelled” to act after the Department of Finance and the Commission on Audit directed it to implement this long-delayed revision, as required under Section 219 of Republic Act 7160, also known as the Local Government Code of 1991. — Reports from Jomar Canlas and Dempsey Reyes

SUNRISE, Fla. — Jonathan Huberdeau scored with 7.7 seconds left in the third period to lift the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 victory over the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday night.
Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad also scored for the Panthers. Harri Sateri made 26 saves for his third straight NHL win. Keith Yandle had two assists.
Danny DeKeyser scored both goals for Detroit and Petr Mrazek stopped 30 shots in his third straight start.
With the score tied at 2, Huberdeau slid a rebound under Mrazek’s pad from inside the crease. The goal was challenged for goalie interference by Detroit but the call stood.
Barkov broke a 1-1 tie with his goal with 6:22 left in the second period. Evgenii Dadanov passed to Barkov in the high slot and Barkov skated in and beat Mrazek on the glove side.
DeKeyser tied it with his second of the game. Sateri blocked a shot and the bouncing puck went off DeKeyser’s skate as he crashed the net and went across the goal line at 3:00 of the third period.
Ekblad’s goal gave the Panthers a 1-0 lead at 3:14 of the first. Ekblad took a pass from Huberdeau in the slot and backhanded the puck off the post and into the net.
DeKeyser tied the score when his shot from the slot went over Sateri’s shoulder on the stick side at 8:51 of the second.
NOTES: Panthers D Alex Petrovic played his 200th NHL game. … Florida F Jamie McGinn returned after missing two games with an upper-body injury. … The Red Wings played their third game in four days. … DeKeyser played his 350th NHL game.
UP NEXT:
Red Wings: Host the Boston Bruins on Tuesday
Panthers: Host the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday.
rewrite:
In a dramatic finish on Saturday night, Jonathan Huberdeau delivered a 3-2 victory for the Florida Panthers over the Detroit Red Wings, scoring with just 7.7 seconds remaining in the third period. The Panthers also saw goals from Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad, while goaltender Harri Sateri secured his third consecutive NHL win with 26 saves. Keith Yandle contributed two assists for Florida.

Detroit’s effort was led by Danny DeKeyser, who netted both goals for the Red Wings. Goaltender Petr Mrazek, making his third straight start, turned aside 30 shots in the losing effort.

The game was tied 2-2 when Huberdeau pounced on a rebound in the crease, sliding the puck under Mrazek’s pad. Detroit challenged the play for goaltender interference, but the goal was upheld after review. Earlier, Barkov had broken a 1-1 deadlock with 6:22 left in the second period, taking a pass from Evgenii Dadanov in the high slot and beating Mrazek on the glove side.

DeKeyser had tied the game for a second time at 3:00 of the third period. After Sateri made an initial save, the puck bounced off DeKeyser’s skate as he drove the net and trickled across the line. Ekblad opened the scoring at 3:14 of the first period, taking a Huberdeau pass and banking a backhand shot off the post. DeKeyser’s first goal, a slot shot over Sateri’s shoulder, had evened the score at 8:51 of the second.

In team notes: Panthers defenseman Alex Petrovic appeared in his 200th NHL game, and forward Jamie McGinn returned from a two-game absence due to an upper-body injury. The Red Wings, playing their third game in four days, saw DeKeyser skate in his 350th career game.

Up next, the Red Wings host the Boston Bruins on Tuesday, while the Panthers welcome the Vancouver Canucks.

May 2 First Solar Inc
* First Solar Inc. Announces first quarter 2017 financial results
* First Solar Inc sees 2017 loss per share of $0.30 to earnings per share of $0.40
* Q1 non-GAAP earnings per share $0.25
* Q1 GAAP earnings per share $0.09
* Q1 sales $892 million
* Q1 revenue view $667.8 million -- Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S
* Q1 earnings per share view $-0.13 -- Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S
* Raises 2017 revenue, EPS, operating cash flow and net cash guidance
* Qtrly net sales increased from prior quarter primarily due to sale of moapa project, partially offset by lower third-party module sales
* First Solar Inc sees 2017 shipments 2.4gw to 2.6gw
* First Solar Inc sees 2017 GAAP net sales of $2.85 billion to $2.95 billion
* First Solar Inc sees 2017 earnings per share non-gaap $0.25 to $0.75
* First Solar Inc sees 2017 gaap gross margin 12.5% to 14.5%
* FY2017 revenue view $2.78 billion -- Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S
* FY2017 earnings per share view $0.32 -- Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S
* First solar inc - "transition to our series 6 product continues to progress from both a technology and commercial standpoint" Source text for Eikon: Further company coverage:
rewrite:
First Solar Inc. released its first-quarter 2017 financial results on May 2. The company reported quarterly net sales of $892 million, a significant increase from the prior quarter. This growth was primarily driven by the sale of the Moapa project, though it was partially offset by lower third-party module sales. On a non-GAAP basis, earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter were $0.25, while GAAP EPS came in at $0.09. These results exceeded analyst expectations, as the Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S consensus had estimated revenue of $667.8 million and a loss per share of $0.13.

Looking ahead, First Solar has updated its full-year 2017 guidance. The company now anticipates GAAP net sales in the range of $2.85 billion to $2.95 billion, with shipments projected between 2.4 and 2.6 gigawatts. For earnings, the forecast ranges from a loss of $0.30 per share to earnings of $0.40 per share on a GAAP basis, while the non-GAAP EPS outlook is between $0.25 and $0.75. The company also raised its guidance for revenue, EPS, operating cash flow, and net cash. The GAAP gross margin is expected to be 12.5% to 14.5%. These projections compare to the analyst consensus of $2.78 billion in revenue and $0.32 EPS for the full year.

First Solar noted that its transition to the Series 6 product line is progressing well from both technological and commercial perspectives.

A Former Marist Brother and Auckland Catholic Diocese employee is facing three historical sex charges against young girls.
Michael Beaumont, 71, appeared in Auckland District Court today facing charges of indecently assaulting two 12-year-old girls and one 9-year-old girl in 1977.
Beaumont entered no plea.
He is listed as administration support for tertiary education provider The Catholic Institute of New Zealand on their website.
Advertisement
"Michael was a teacher for many years and is now working part time for TCI in a support role and part time for the Auckland Diocese in a similar role for the RE [religious education] Team.
"He has also, since its inception, been involved as a member of the team fielding calls to the Family Violence Information Line, part of the "It's not OK" campaign helping to increase awareness around family violence and abuse," Beaumont's employee description said.
Beaumont formerly worked part-time for the Auckland Catholic Diocese.
He will next appear in court on June 21.

Beaumont is listed on its website as providing administrative support for The Catholic Institute of New Zealand, a tertiary education provider. Qantas has no plans to alter its flight schedule to Exmouth, despite mounting evidence planes have been filling up all year, resulting in higher prices and limited travel options for residents and tourists.
The Shire of Exmouth and Exmouth Chamber of Commerce and Industry has been lobbying the national carrier to boost capacity, with chamber president Barry Sullivan stating evidence suggested current services were above 80 per cent capacity.
Shire president Matthew Niikkula said long-term commitment to increased flight capacity would support investment and jobs growth in Exmouth.
“Qantas and Tourism Australia are using the Ningaloo Reef experience to support the campaign to attract visitors to Australia,” he said.
“Providing additional ongoing seating capacity to Exmouth will make sure people can access that experience they are being promised.
“The first step is to have a commitment to additional flights, and to date that has not happened outside ad hoc, short-term measures such as one-off increases during the coming school holidays.”
Mr Niikkula said bigger planes, additional flights or provision of an Exmouth to Broome link would be beneficial.
QANTAS has slashed airfares from Perth to Broome in a bid to get more people heading to WA's north instead of Bali. The West Australian Video QANTAS has slashed airfares from Perth to Broome in a bid to get more people heading to WA's north instead of Bali.
Qantas refused to confirm the capacity of flights to and from Exmouth, claiming the average amount of people on a plane was commercially sensitive information.
“We currently have no plans to change our schedule for flights to Learmonth, however we are always reviewing our network to ensure that we have the right aircraft on the right route to match demand,” a spokeswoman said.
North West Central MLA Vince Catania said the State Government needed to push airlines to be more honest with the public.
“The Government should be demanding Qantas puts on extra flights as a requirement of their licence,” he said.
“Airlines look at load factor and how they can maximise profits to benefit them, rather than looking at capacity for the community.
“This is not just about reducing airfares, it is about the company being open and transparent on how they come up with their ticket price.”
Mr Catania said Exmouth fares should be capped at $150.
rewrite:
Despite consistent evidence that flights to Exmouth have been operating at high capacity throughout the year—leading to elevated fares and limited options for both residents and visitors—Qantas has indicated it will not be adjusting its flight schedule to the region. Local advocacy from the Shire of Exmouth and the Exmouth Chamber of Commerce and Industry has been ongoing, with chamber president Barry Sullivan noting that data suggests current services are consistently above 80 percent capacity.

Shire President Matthew Niikkula emphasized that a long-term commitment to increased flight capacity would foster investment and job growth in Exmouth. He pointed out that Qantas and Tourism Australia are actively promoting the Ningaloo Reef experience to attract international visitors to Australia. “Ensuring additional, ongoing seating capacity to Exmouth would guarantee that people can actually access the experience they are being promised,” Niikkula stated. “The first step is a firm commitment to extra flights, but so far, we’ve only seen short-term, ad-hoc measures, like one-off increases during upcoming school holidays.”

Niikkula added that solutions could include larger aircraft, additional flight frequencies, or even establishing a direct air link between Exmouth and Broome. This suggestion comes amid Qantas’s recent move to slash airfares from Perth to Broome, an effort to redirect travelers toward Western Australia’s north instead of destinations like Bali.

However, Qantas has declined to disclose specific load factors for Exmouth flights, describing average passenger numbers as commercially sensitive information. A spokeswoman said, “We currently have no plans to change our schedule for flights to Learmonth [Exmouth’s airport], but we continually review our network to ensure we match the right aircraft to the right routes based on demand.”

Weighing in on the issue, North West Central MLA Vince Catania argued that the State Government should pressure airlines to be more transparent with the public. “The Government ought to require Qantas to add extra flights as a condition of their licence,” Catania said. He criticized airlines for prioritizing load factors and profit maximization over community needs for adequate capacity. “This isn’t just about lowering airfares—it’s about the company being open and transparent regarding how they determine ticket prices.” Catania went so far as to propose that Exmouth fares should be capped at $150 to ensure affordability and access.

The iconic “Hollywood” sign got a New Year’s Day makeover from an unknown vandal who used a black tarp to transform the letters into a message celebrating marijuana.
Multiple social media images showed the new “Hollyweed” sign on Mount Lee overlooking Los Angeles. One of the black tarps appeared to have an image of a peace symbol and the other a heart.
Cops have surveillance video of the suspect, TMZ reported. The vandal, dressed in all black, could face a misdemeanor trespassing charge, said Sgt. Robert Payan. The person scaled a protective fence surrounding the sign and then clambered up each giant letter to drape the coverings, Payan said.
California in November passed a measure legalizing marijuana for recreational use.
Though the Prop 64 vote may have been an impetus to change the sign, it wouldn’t be the first time someone has taken to the hills to alter the letters in honor of cannabis. A vandal also changed the sign to read “Hollyweed” on New Year’s Day 1976, TMZ reported.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
rewrite:
The iconic Hollywood sign received an unsanctioned New Year's Day update when an unidentified individual used black tarps to alter the letters, turning the landmark into "Hollyweed" in a nod to marijuana. Social media posts showed the modified sign overlooking Los Angeles from Mount Lee, with one tarp featuring a peace symbol and another a heart. According to TMZ, police have surveillance footage of the suspect, who was dressed entirely in black. Sergeant Robert Payan stated the vandal could face misdemeanor trespassing charges for scaling the protective fence and climbing each massive letter to attach the coverings.

This act follows California's November passage of a measure legalizing recreational cannabis. While the Prop 64 vote may have inspired the alteration, it is not without precedent: as TMZ noted, a similar change was made to the sign on New Year's Day in 1976, also spelling "Hollyweed." The Associated Press contributed to this report.

FRANKLIN COUNTY, KY (WAVE) – An elderly Franklin County woman was removed from her home after police say they found her living in deplorable conditions.
The woman, who has not been identified, lived on Stable Lane in Frankfort. Police say they were notified after the Humane Society called them.
The Human Society says they received a tip, stating a bunch of animals were living in the home. When workers went to the home for a welfare check, they called Animal Control and the Sheriff's Department.

Inside the home, deputies found 18 cats and nine dogs living in the home with the woman and her adult daughter. They found the elderly woman lying on the floor in animal feces. Deputies said the stench in the home was so horrid, they had to wear masks.
"I can honestly say the condition of the home was the worst I have ever seen," said deputy Chris Eaton. "The floors and the walls were covered with animal feces."

rewrite:
In Franklin County, Kentucky, an elderly woman was removed from her home after authorities discovered her living in what they described as deplorable conditions. According to police, the woman was found lying on the floor amid animal feces. The investigation began when the Humane Society contacted law enforcement after receiving a tip about numerous animals residing at the home on Stable Lane in Frankfort. During a welfare check, Humane Society workers alerted both Animal Control and the Sheriff’s Department.

Inside the residence, deputies encountered 18 cats and nine dogs living with the woman and her adult daughter. The stench was so overwhelming that officers had to wear masks. Deputy Chris Eaton stated, “I can honestly say the condition of the home was the worst I have ever seen. The floors and the walls were covered with animal feces.” While the animals were reported to be in good health, authorities noted the situation as particularly sad, observing that the pets appeared to have been the priority.

Social Services is now investigating, and the daughter may face neglect charges. The elderly woman, who has not been publicly identified, was taken from the home for her safety and well-being.

"We just wanted to know what happened, and with the Russian attack so recent, we feared the worst," said Edwards.

Britain has accused Russia of poisoning the Skripals with Novichok, a nerve agent belonging to a class of chemical weapons developed by the Soviet Union during the Cold War. Rep. Tim Murphy (R-PA), who announced his resignation from Congress Thursday, reportedly ran a office rife with the mistreatment of staffers.
Before his resignation, the vocally pro-life Pennsylvania Republican was revealed to have asked a mistress to get an abortion.
Politico reported the behavior on Thursday, following Murphy’s announcement of his resignation. The outlet reported that a potential investigation into Murphy’s treatment of his employees by the House Ethics Committee motivated his resignation as much as the revelations about his mistress.
Multiple unnamed former Murphy staffers told Politico that the behavior of the congressman’s chief of staff, Susan Mosychuk, had moved them to quit.
“It was one of the worst places I have ever worked in my life. There was screaming. Intimidation. Nothing you ever did was right,” a former Murphy district director, Nick Rodondo, told Pittsburgh radio station KDKA, Politico noted.
Every other source was unnamed: Politico reported that Mosychuk called staffers “worthless” and their work “garbage.”
“It’s not like a private company where you have an HR department,” one former staffer told Politico. “It was a culture of abuse and a culture of corruption. There really is no oversight.”
“Screaming was an everyday thing,” said another unnamed former staffer. “The manipulation and the mind games. … Everybody in that office was depressed.”
Multiple unnamed ex-staffers told the publication the chief of staff used white noise machines placed around the congressman’s office in order to mask the sound of her screaming. Staffers were told to take the stairs instead of the elevator as a punishment, according to one former employee, and bathroom breaks were cut short in order to administer verbal disciplining.
Politico also reported that a leaked June 2017 memo by Mosychuk, called “Office Conduct and Behavior: Harassment/Legal Compliance” and outlining supposed abusive behavior by the congressman, more accurately described Mosychuk’s own behavior.
“She was the one who would verbally abuse staff,” one unnamed ex-staffer said. “He was bad, but you can deal with a tough member. She was literally terrorizing people.”
Read Politico’s full story here.
rewrite:
Congressman Tim Murphy, a Republican from Pennsylvania, announced his resignation on Thursday amid reports that his office was rife with mistreatment of staff. The vocally pro-life lawmaker had previously been revealed to have urged a mistress to seek an abortion, but according to a Politico report published the same day, his decision to step down was driven as much by a potential House Ethics Committee investigation into his office’s workplace environment as by that personal scandal.

Multiple former staffers, most speaking anonymously, described a toxic atmosphere under Murphy’s chief of staff, Susan Mosychuk. Nick Rodondo, a former district director for Murphy, told Pittsburgh radio station KDKA, “It was one of the worst places I have ever worked in my life. There was screaming. Intimidation. Nothing you ever did was right.” Other former employees echoed these sentiments to Politico, alleging that Mosychuk routinely belittled staff, calling them “worthless” and their work “garbage.”

The office culture was characterized as abusive and oppressive. “Screaming was an everyday thing,” one unnamed former staffer said. “The manipulation and the mind games. … Everybody in that office was depressed.” Another pointed out the lack of recourse, noting, “It’s not like a private company where you have an HR department. It was a culture of abuse and a culture of corruption. There really is no oversight.”

Disturbing details emerged about efforts to conceal the hostility. According to several ex-staffers, white noise machines were placed around the congressman’s office to muffle the sound of Mosychuk’s yelling. Punitive measures allegedly included forcing staff to use the stairs instead of the elevator and cutting bathroom breaks short to administer verbal reprimands.

Ironically, a June 2017 memo authored by Mosychuk—titled “Office Conduct and Behavior: Harassment/Legal Compliance” and outlining abusive behavior—was described by former employees as a more accurate portrait of her own conduct. “She was the one who would verbally abuse staff,” one ex-staffer said. “He was bad, but you can deal with a tough member. She was literally terrorizing people.”

The team of contractors arrived in the detention center and had already arranged the list of interviews with the migrants detained in the Australian facility, the ABC Online news outlet reported Tuesday.
The media outlet added that there would be about 20 interviews per day during a month.
Australia detains refugees who come to the country to seek asylum in offshore detention camps, while their application is being processed by the authorities. Such measures have been repeatedly criticized by different rights groups.
In November 2016, then-US President Barack Obama and Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull concluded a one-time deal to resettle refugees, currently detained in Australian processing centers on the Manus Island and Nauru in the South Pacific.
However the agreement had been reportedly criticized by the incumbent US President Donald Trump and several media suggested that the deal could be terminated.

Lucy Durack on set, on her first day of filming Lift
Lucy Durack on set, on her first day of filming Lift Picture: Ian Munro
It was an odd encounter in the lift at her daughter’s day care that led Lucy Durack home to Perth — and to her debut as a screenwriter.
Durack, an acclaimed theatre actress, will spend much of this week inside a makeshift wooden elevator inside a small film studio in Maylands, shooting Lift, a romantic comedy web series she created and wrote.
Sydney-based Durack, best known for her award-winning turns as Glinda the Good Witch in Wicked and Elle Woods in Legally Blonde: The Musical, said seeing her script come to life was “incredibly, overwhelmingly fun”.
Durack penned five comedies with her writing partners, brother and sister duo Jess and Leon Murray, but they settled on Lift partly because of its format of seven four-minute episodes.
The story follows Olivia (Durack) on her way to a job interview and Simon (theatre actor Duncan Ragg), who is about to propose to his girlfriend, and their fateful meeting in an elevator.
“I love a romantic comedy ... and this one came out of a fairly awkward conversation I had with a stranger in a lift at my daughter’s day care,” Durack laughed.
Actress and singer Lucy Durack is back home in Perth visiting her family for a week. She is also appearing in new Nine series Doctor Doctor. Picture: Ian Munro
“We wanted something we could make on a small budget, before we got funding from Screenwest.
“The rules were each episode was one lift ride and there was one location, so we had to stretch the boundaries to make it into a real romantic comedy, just in microscopic form.”
And when Lift goes online midyear, it will be the culmination of tireless work by “an incredible team of up-and-coming WA crew and volunteers”, according to producer Lauren Elliott.
WA’s Zoe Pepper is directing and Chloe Rickard is executive producer. As Durack points out, it is an all-female line-up at the helm. “It’s just cool to be on a set with so many women,” she said. “It’s really inspiring and exciting.”
rewrite:
Lucy Durack is spending much of her week inside a makeshift wooden elevator in a Maylands film studio, shooting *Lift*, the romantic comedy web series she created and wrote. This project marks her debut as a screenwriter, a journey that began with an awkward encounter in a lift at her daughter’s daycare—an experience that ultimately helped bring her back home to Perth.

The Sydney-based actress, acclaimed for her award-winning stage roles as Glinda in *Wicked* and Elle Woods in *Legally Blonde: The Musical*, describes seeing her script come to life as “incredibly, overwhelmingly fun.” *Lift* follows Olivia (played by Durack) and Simon (theatre actor Duncan Ragg) as their paths cross in an elevator—she’s on her way to a job interview, he’s about to propose—turning a routine lift ride into a fateful meeting.

Durack developed the series with writing partners Jess and Leon Murray, settling on this concept partly for its practical format: seven four-minute episodes, each set within a single elevator ride. “We wanted something we could make on a small budget,” she explained. “The rules were one location per episode, so we had to stretch the boundaries to create a real romantic comedy in microscopic form.”

When *Lift* launches online midyear, it will represent the culmination of dedicated work by what producer Lauren Elliott calls “an incredible team of up-and-coming WA crew and volunteers.” The production is led by an all-female creative team, with Zoe Pepper directing and Chloe Rickard as executive producer. “It’s just cool to be on a set with so many women,” Durack noted. “It’s really inspiring and exciting.”

Currently in Perth visiting family, Durack is also appearing in the new Nine series *Doctor Doctor*. But for now, her focus is on the tiny studio elevator, where a brief, real-life moment has been transformed into a charming fictional romance.

The world of Batman has seen several poignant moments recently, reflecting on its legacy while celebrating its enduring spirit. Benjamin Melniker, the legendary producer without whom the iconic film series might never have existed, has passed away at 104. In a separate tribute to the superhero's origins, a street near Poe Park in the Bronx will be renamed “Bill Finger Way” this Friday, finally granting the late, unsung co-creator a lasting public honor.

Meanwhile, the current Batman, Ben Affleck, remains committed to the role despite playful rumors from his brother Casey, confirming last month he has no plans to leave the franchise. The caped crusader's influence continues to inspire acts of heroism off-screen as well. A police officer in Fort Worth, Texas, regularly transforms into Batman to bring joy to ailing children across the country, and another Fort Worth officer dressed as the Dark Knight recently made a memorable appearance at a local Walmart.

The recent passing of Adam West, the beloved star of the 1960s "Batman" series, has also been met with reflection and tribute. His co-star Burt Ward shared that West "had no idea" he was dying, recalling their final cheerful meeting just weeks prior. To honor West’s legacy, Los Angeles Mayor Eric Garcetti will light the Bat-Signal at City Hall, a fitting tribute to the man who first brought Batman to life for a generation.

CHARLOTTE, North Carolina, Aug 12 (Reuters) - Hideki Matsuyama has broad shoulders but is not finding it easy to carry the weight of an entire nation as he seeks to become the first Japanese man to win a major.
Matsuyama started the third round of the PGA Championship tied for the lead with Kevin Kisner but never got into gear, a bogey at the first setting the table for a pedestrian one-over-par 72.
That was still good enough to remain in contention, a stroke behind Kisner, who dropped three shots in the final three holes.
"Probably the pressure had something to do with it, being in the last group in a major tournament," said Matsuyama.
"But I haven't been spot-on all week, and the worries I had about my swing showed up today in the way I played.
"I'm disappointed the way I played today, however I'm happy to be one stroke back and still have a chance and looking forward to tomorrow."
Matsuyama is coming off a closing 61 that clinched a runaway victory at last week's WGC-Bridgestone Invitational. He said at the time he had shot the stunning score despite being uncomfortable with his swing, words he repeated pre-tournament here.
Despite his struggles, the 25-year-old played the difficult final three holes better than his rivals, parring them all to finish the day much closer than he expected an hour previously.
rewrite:
CHARLOTTE, North Carolina, Aug 12 (Reuters) - Hideki Matsuyama carries the hopes of a nation on his broad shoulders, a weight that proved heavy as he vied to become the first Japanese man to win a major championship.

Beginning the third round of the PGA Championship tied for the lead with Kevin Kisner, Matsuyama never found his rhythm. An opening bogey set the tone for a sluggish one-over-par 72. Despite this, he remained firmly in contention, just one stroke behind Kisner, who stumbled with three dropped shots over the final three holes.

"Being in the final group of a major, the pressure probably played a part," Matsuyama admitted. "My game hasn't been sharp all week, and the doubts about my swing surfaced in my play today. While I'm disappointed with how I performed, I'm happy to be only one shot back and still have a chance. I'm looking forward to tomorrow."

This performance follows a spectacular final-round 61 that secured a dominant win at last week's WGC-Bridgestone Invitational. Notably, Matsuyama had said then—and repeated before this tournament—that he posted that stunning score despite feeling uneasy with his swing.

Even on a difficult day, the 25-year-old showed resilience. He navigated the challenging final three holes better than his rivals, parring each one to end the day much closer to the lead than he had anticipated just an hour before.

During CBS’ coverage of the shooting at a Congressional baseball practice, anchor Charlie Rose stated, “people talk about things like ‘lock her up,’ and we saw some of the most crude political language that we’d heard. … This has been a season of sort of coarse political rhetoric.”
Rose said, “[W]e saw during the time that members went back home, because of some of the debates in Congress, they were particularly raucous town meetings, not about threats to their lives, but clearly, the level in combativeness was more apparent than ever.”
He later added, after Congressional Correspondent Nancy Cordes said that it can be difficult for members of Congress to tell who is merely exercising their free speech rights and someone who has the intent of committing violence, “Clearly, we saw that during the campaign, which people talk about things like ‘lock her up,’ and we saw some of the most crude political language that we’d heard, even though there’s a long history of political attacks in American politics since the Founding Fathers. We did see expressions that we had not heard before. This has been a season of sort of coarse political rhetoric.”
Follow Ian Hanchett on Twitter @IanHanchett
rewrite:
During CBS's coverage of the shooting at a Congressional baseball practice, anchor Charlie Rose remarked on the increasingly harsh tone of political discourse. He noted that phrases like "lock her up" and other crude language had become prominent, describing it as "a season of sort of coarse political rhetoric." Rose pointed out that when members of Congress returned to their districts, town hall meetings grew particularly raucous, not due to direct threats, but because the level of combativeness was more apparent than ever.

Later, after Congressional Correspondent Nancy Cordes observed that it can be hard for lawmakers to distinguish between free speech and genuine violent intent, Rose expanded on his point. He reflected that during the recent campaign, there were expressions of political hostility unlike any heard before, despite America's long history of political attacks dating back to the Founding Fathers. This period, he reiterated, has been marked by unusually coarse rhetoric.

PRINCETON, N.J. — Jerome Desrosiers’ 3-pointer with 36 seconds left in overtime provided the winning points in Princeton’s 76-73 victory over Yale on Friday.
After Desrosiers’ trey, Yale missed consecutive 3-point shots and fouled Amir Bell, who missed the front end of a one-and-one. The teams exchanged turnovers before a desperation 3-point try by Yale missed.
Yale took possession after a tie-up in regulation but Trey Phills was unable to connect on a 3-pointer as the game went to overtime.
Myles Stephens scored 18 points and Devin Cannady and Bell 16 apiece for the Tigers (11-8, 3-1 Ivy), who have won three straight, with Bell collecting a career-high 11 rebounds for his first career double-double.
Alex Copeland scored 18 points, Phills had 17 points and a career-high 14 rebounds for his first career double-double while Blake Reynolds added 15 points for the Bulldogs (9-12, 2-3).
rewrite:
In a thrilling overtime finish, Jerome Desrosiers sank a crucial three-pointer with just 36 seconds remaining, lifting Princeton to a 76-73 victory over Yale on Friday. After Desrosiers' shot, Yale missed two consecutive three-point attempts and fouled Amir Bell, who missed the front end of a one-and-one free throw opportunity. Following exchanged turnovers, a final desperation three from Yale fell short. The game had been forced into overtime after Yale gained possession from a tie-up in regulation, only for Trey Phills to miss a three-point attempt at the buzzer.

For Princeton (11-8, 3-1 Ivy), now on a three-game winning streak, Myles Stephens led with 18 points, while Devin Cannady and Amir Bell each added 16. Bell also secured a career-high 11 rebounds for his first double-double. Yale (9-12, 2-3) was paced by Alex Copeland with 18 points. Phills contributed 17 points and a career-best 14 rebounds for his own first double-double, and Blake Reynolds chipped in 15 points.

Talk about living up to your name.
A Florida woman named Crystal Methvin was arrested Saturday in St. Johns County on drug possession charges after being caught with crystal meth, jail records show.
Methvin, 40, of St. Augustine, was busted after an anonymous caller tipped off cops who found her inside a car with two other people in a parking lot on South Dixie Highway, WJXT reports.
Police searched the car and found drug paraphernalia and a substance that tested positive for crystal meth.
Methvin was taken into custody with a man identified as Douglas Nickerson, WJXT reports.
Methvin has arrests in the county dating back to 1998 when she was booked into the St. Johns County Jail for driving under the influence. Most recently, she was arrested in January on 14 felony counts of drug possession and misdemeanor possession of drug equipment, jail records show.
Methvin remains in custody on $5,000 bond, according to jail records. It’s unclear if she’s hired an attorney.
rewrite:
Sometimes a name can be eerily fitting. Crystal Methvin, a 40-year-old woman from St. Augustine, Florida, was arrested on drug charges this past Saturday in St. Johns County after police found her in possession of crystal methamphetamine. According to jail records and local news station WJXT, the arrest followed an anonymous tip that led officers to a car in a parking lot on South Dixie Highway. Inside the vehicle, occupied by Methvin and two others, police discovered drug paraphernalia and a substance that later tested positive for crystal meth. She was taken into custody alongside a man identified as Douglas Nickerson.

Methvin’s history with local law enforcement stretches back to 1998 with a DUI arrest. Most recently, in January, she faced 14 felony drug possession counts along with a misdemeanor for possessing drug equipment. She is currently being held on a $5,000 bond, and it is not yet known if she has legal representation.

TAIPEI, April 12 Taiwan stocks fell along with other regional bourses on Wednesday as investors favoured safe-haven assets in response to geopolitical tensions, with heavyweights such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) down ahead of quarterly results.
The main TAIEX index fell 0.4 percent to 9,793.12 points as of 0141 GMT, after closing at 9,832.42 points.
The electronics subindex dropped 0.4 percent, while the financials subindex lost 0.2 percent.
TSMC, the world's top contract chipmaker and an Apple Inc supplier, fell 0.5 percent.
The company is set to report its first-quarter results on Thursday. Analysts have been concerned that the local currency's appreciation against the U.S. dollar could weigh on its earnings.
The Taiwan dollar firmed T$0.008 to T$30.642 per U.S. dollar on Wednesday. (Reporting by Faith Hung; Editing by Amrutha Gayathri)

JOSE MOURINHO WAS spotted at a friendly between Austria and Russia on Wednesday, as rumours swirl he is targeting a move for Austrian forward Marko Arnautovic.
The West Ham star has been linked with a big money move to the north of England as Mourinho looks to bring in reinforcements for Manchester United behind Romelu Lukaku.
The pair previously worked together in 2009-10 at Inter, when Arnautovic was on loan from Twente, but the move did not work out.
The forward only appeared in three Serie A contests as a substitute, with Mourinho saying the striker had “the mentality of a child” and claimed he was “unmanageable”.
However, that was eight years ago, and the 29-year-old Arnautovic has displayed quality since then, scoring 11 goals last season for West Ham after making a £20 million move from Stoke City, where he had spent the previous four seasons. He also added six assists in his 31 Premier League appearances
It was the second time in three seasons Arnautovic had scored 11 goals and added six assists, having managed it with Stoke in 2015-16.
Those numbers have led to speculation Mourinho could seek to add him to play with or beside Lukaku after the Red Devils’ depth behind the Belgian was proven wanting in the 1-0 FA Cup loss to Chelsea .
And Mourinho’s presence at a friendly in which Arnautovic started is only likely to pour more fuel on the rumour fire despite Mourinho reportedly claiming he was only “on holiday” when asked why he was in attendance at Innsbruck
However, if Mourinho was there to have a look at the forward, he was treated to Arnautovic making an impact for his national side as he laid on the assist for Alessandro Schopf’s 28th minute opener.
That proved to be the winner as Arnautovic played 83 minutes of the victory over the World Cup hosts.

rewrite:

The pair have a shared history from the 2009–10 season at Inter Milan, when Arnautovic arrived on loan from Twente. That stint, however, was short-lived and largely unsuccessful. The forward made only three substitute appearances in Serie A, with Mourinho later criticizing his immature attitude, famously describing him as having "the mentality of a child" and deeming him "unmanageable."

But that was eight years ago. Now 29, Arnautovic has since matured and demonstrated his quality in the Premier League. After a £20 million move from Stoke City—where he spent four seasons—he scored 11 goals and provided six assists in 31 league appearances for West Ham last season. Notably, it was the second time in three campaigns he had reached those exact figures, having also recorded 11 goals and six assists for Stoke in 2015–16.

These consistent performances have led to rumors that Mourinho may look to bring him to Old Trafford, especially after United’s lack of depth behind Lukaku was exposed in their 1–0 FA Cup final loss to Chelsea. Mourinho’s presence at a match where Arnautovic started only adds to the speculation, despite the manager’s explanation that he was merely "on holiday" when questioned about his attendance in Innsbruck.

If Mourinho was indeed there to scout the forward, he would have seen Arnautovic make a meaningful contribution. The striker provided the assist for Alessandro Schöpf’s 28th-minute opening goal, which ultimately proved to be the winner in Austria’s victory over World Cup hosts Russia. Arnautovic played 83 minutes of the match, further showcasing the form that has made him a subject of transfer talk.
